articleTitle: IoT-Based Real-Time Monitoring And Control System for Distribution Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents the development and deployment of an IoT-based monitoring and automatic control system for power substations to address equipment failures, energy losses, and safety concerns. This system utilizes a network of sensors to collect voltage, current, and temperature data from various substation components in real-time. The collected data is then sent to a centralized control center and a user-friendly Blynk IoT application that authorized personnel can access. Utilizing sophisticated analytics and algorithms enables proactive maintenance by identifying potential malfunctions and initiating prompt actions. In addition, the system maximizes resource utilization by monitoring voltage levels and balancing loads. Integration with the Blynk application enables remote monitoring, real-time alerts, and remote-control capabilities, thereby improving accessibility and expediting responses to urgent situations. Results show that the proposed system compared to existing ones, improves the substation’s efficiency, minimizes downtime, and increases grid reliability, thereby contributing to more resilient and sustainable power infrastructure.

articleTitle: Long Term Electrical Energy Planning Using LEAP: A Case Study for Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper employs the Long-term Energy Alternative Planning (LEAP) model to investigate the complex energy dynamics of Bangladesh, shedding light on its current energy situation, future electricity demand, and the potential for renewable energy sources. The research examines three distinct scenarios: the business-as-usual (BAU), energy-efficient scenario (EES), and alternative energy scenario (AES). The BAU scenario aligns with the government's planned expansion of energy capacity, while the EES emphasizes energy efficiency through the adoption of efficient devices across households, industries, and the commercial sector. In contrast, the AES focuses on significantly increasing renewable energy utilization, aiming to generate 60% of electricity from sustainable sources, thus reducing reliance on fossil fuels. This study underscores the critical role of sustainable energy solutions in driving economic development, especially in developing nations like Bangladesh. The findings reveal that the status quo in the country's energy system is unsustainable, marked by rising greenhouse gas emissions and heavy dependence on imported fossil fuels. To address these challenges, the research advocates for diversifying the energy mix, investing in renewables, and embracing energy-efficient technologies. This case study serves as a valuable guide for Bangladesh's journey towards a sustainable, secure, and efficient energy future, highlighting the urgency of addressing energy challenges to ensure the country's long-term economic and environmental well-being.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Grid Integrated Bifacial Solar Energy System for Dhaka-Mawa Expressway
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a grid-integrated technical, economic and environmental evaluation of a Bifacial solar system installed along the Dhaka-Mawa Express Highway in Bangladesh. The research intends to study the viability of the Bifacial solar PV system, including issues such as system design, site selection, installation, operation, and maintenance expenses employing the PVsyst simulation software. The study also evaluates the potential energy generation and financial returns of the system. A simulation model is used for the techno-economic assessment of the Bifacial solar PV system. The simulation results indicate that a Bifacial solar PV system installed along the Dhaka Mawa Express Highway has the potential to generate a total of 59.87 GWh/year of electricity. Furthermore, the average monthly output of 4.24 GWh shows how consistently the suggested system produces electricity throughout the year. It is estimated that installing a Bifacial solar PV system will cost a total of USD 25712524 and the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) is USD 0.072. Furthermore, a significant advantage of the Bifacial solar PV system is the total CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> savings of 870510 tonnes over a 25 year period. This is a significant amount of energy that can contribute to reducing the reliance on fossil fuels in the region.

articleTitle: Development of a Single-Phase Hybrid Quadratic AC-DC Boost Converter with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This research presents a novel hybrid AC-DC Boost converter topology. The positive aspects of AC-DC conversion methods are combined in the proposed converter architecture to provide effective power transmission and enhanced grid compatibility. The circuit operations of the proposed converter are also described in detail. The performance of the converter has been evaluated with both the open-loop and closed-loop simulation models. The proposed circuit shows higher voltage gain performance by maintaining other factors including efficiency, total harmonic distortion (THD) and power factor (PF) within a good range. For open loop operation, the suggested converter offers conversion efficiencies of up to 99.77%. The performance of THD percentage shows remarkable result that is lower than the conventional circuit, while PF remains high for a wide range of operations. In closed-loop analysis, we achieved near unity (0.99) PF, more than 99% efficiency and lower THD than the conventional circuit.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of PV Simulation Software by Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This study employs the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) methodology to evaluate and compare four prominent PV simulation software tools: PVsyst, HOMER, PVGIS, and SAM. With the urgent need to transition to renewable energy due to escalating global warming concerns, the evaluation of simulation software becomes pivotal. Each software tool is assessed based on criteria such as availability and cost, solar database access, input data requirements, output presentation, updateability, and limitations. A comprehensive AHP hierarchy is established and pair-wise comparisons are performed to assign relative priorities. The weights of each criterion are determined, leading to an overall rating for each software. The results reveal that SAM is the most suitable choice for Bangladesh due to its cost-effectiveness, extensive solar database, efficient input requirements, comprehensive output analysis, and adaptability. This research provides valuable insights for decision-makers in selecting an appropriate PV simulation software tool to promote renewable energy adoption and planning.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT) based Smart Grid Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Smart Grid and the Internet of Things (IoT) are riveting topics of the modern era. Integrating them makes it even more compelling. The power transmission process as a whole will increase its resiliency in consequence. And we will be one step closer to the era of Smart cities. This paper proposes a prototype of a Grid management system that converts any traditional Power Grid into a Smart Grid. The Smart Grid Management System has the features: a power monitoring system, billing system, theft detection system, remote switching, personal and grid power monitoring websites, cloud storage, dynamic graphs, and emergency backup power supply. The system uses sensors to measure the power consumed and current through a load. The readings are sent to the cloud that can be displayed on personal and grid websites. Remote switching features are added to control the continuation of the power supply for both users and grid members. In-house displays are installed in each unit for users to be conscious of their power usage. The system also detects and alerts if there is any illegal power usage. Finally, the system has a backup solar power supply in case of power shortage or outage.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fuel Saving for Merit Order Based Load Curtailment Profile in 5 Bus Power System Network
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Without electricity no one can think of economic development of a country. Besides per-capita electricity consumption has become an important parameter for the measurement of development of a country. On the other hand the fuel/resources that are needed to generate electricity are limited. There are several global and domestic factors which lead to increase in fuel price and it becomes difficult to import more fuels. In addition to it as the fossil fuels are the primary source of energy, it is running out rapidly. Thereby we have to meet the electricity demand (load) with these limited resources. One of the common ways to sustain more days with these limited fuels is load curtailment. This load curtailment should effective such that for same amount load curtailment we can sustain more days. In this research work the PJM 5 bus system is used which commonly used for power system economic study. As a load the daily load curve of Bangladesh is used and the optimal power flow (OPF) problem is solved using Lagrangian method. In this paper we investigate different load curtailment profile to save fuel and merit order based load curtailment method is proposed which will save more fuel than flat load curtailment. Using the merit order based load curtailment method it is found that in case of 10% merit order based load curtailment, for every 4.5 days of operation we run one more day and in case of 20% merit order based load curtailment, for every 1.77 days of operation we run one more day.

articleTitle: Rate of Change of Frequency(RoCoF) Improvement of Low Inertia Power System by Using Refrigerated Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The frequency regulation is a critical concern in modern power systems due to the penetration of the wind and solar power plants as renewable energy sources (RESs), resulting in the reduction of inertia of generating units. Due to the short time duration and less operation cost, primary frequency regulation is given priority to low inertia grid to prevent from collapse or blackout along with reducing rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). Thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) provide a significant spinning reserve due to their thermal inertia. Potato plays a vital role in food chain worldwide. For lack of preservation, the quality of potatoes is degraded and rot. In this proposed work, the rate of change of frequency of low inertia area of a two-area system is improved by using centralized direct load control of a population of potato cold storage for sudden power unbalance. A design of potato cold storage for this work is proposed. The virtual synchronous machine with cold storage model is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink in the proposed work. Different case studies prove the potential of using this method to improve rate of change of frequency in primary frequency regulation. In the proposed approach, the user’s comfort is sacrificed for very short time operation. The incentives given to customers to participate in demand response (DR) program by proposed method emphasizes the future work on different control strategies for fast frequency regulation.

articleTitle: A Reduced Component Count MLI for Solar Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this work, a reduced component count multilevel inverter (RCCMLI) topology of only six switches and two DC sources is proposed, which is simulated in high frequency-based Multi-Carrier Pulse Width Modulation Techniques (MCPWM). As the conventional converters add more switches and component counts including high THD output, reduced component count topology is proposed in this paper. Besides, high-frequency control with asymmetrical DC inputs uplifts the output voltage level for the selected inverter. The proposed inverter is analyzed for both single and three-phase modes for four types of MCPWM strategies such as Phase Disposition (PD), Phase Opposition Disposition (POD), Alternate Phase Opposition Disposition (APOD), and variable Frequency PWM (VFPWM). Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) achieved for different methodologies of MCPWM is comparatively shown in the simulation and results section. For single-phase simulation voltage, THD is 9.03% with seven-level output, and for three-phase current THD is 1.63% with thirteen-level output. The simulated single and three-phase inverters can be used for solar power generation, especially for stand-alone and grid-connected applications.

articleTitle: Energy Commitment in Prosumer-Centric P2P Energy Trading via Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In a smart grid era, blockchain technology is one of the most feasible mechanisms to encourage prosumers to participate in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading in local distributed energy markets. However, the fair evaluation and the prosumer’s enthusiasm to participate in energy trading are the major challenges in P2P energy trading. Therefore, enhancing the reliability of P2P energy trading is a vital issue for local distributed energy markets. In this study, a novel peer matching mechanism is developed, which is based on blockchain technology and covers ‘one-to-one’ and ‘one-to-many’ matching among prosumers during the local energy trading market. Firstly, individual prosumers’ data is shared by accessing the web portal with their individual login credentials to the blockchain trading platform. Secondly, peer matching is performed based on the reliability score of individual participants, which is computed from the prosumer’s energy commitment. Finally, based on mid-market rate mechanisms, P2P energy trading is included in the blockchain framework. This use case study demonstrates that the proposed mechanism encourages prosumers to participate fearlessly and scope for improving their energy commitment in the peer matching process as it does not include any monetary fines or incentives to the prosumers. Also, it has an exceptionally good computational performance and scalability to inspire energy trading at the local distribution level.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell Using Alternanthera dentata Natural Dye
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A dye-sensitized solar cell harnesses solar radiation to generate electrical power through sensitization of the cell. The efficacy of these solar cells is primarily contingent upon the specific dye employed as the sensitizing agent. In this research, a spin-coated nanocrystalline TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> photo-electrode was successfully employed on a glass substrate coated with SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>:F. A dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) was fabricated using a natural dye extracted from Alternanthera dentata leaves as the photosensitizing agent. The carbon back electrode and KI/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based electrolyte solution were the other components of this DSSC. 685 mV open circuit voltage (Voc), 0.568 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> short circuit current density (Jsc), 43.05% fill factor (FF), and 0.1675% efficiency was observed in the case of Alternanthera dentata dye-sensitized solar cell. This dye is readily available throughout Bangladesh and provides affordability, eco-friendliness, and simple dye extraction benefits.

articleTitle: Controller Hardware-In-the-Loop Validation of Phasor-Domain Algorithms for High-Speed Protection of Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Controller hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) validation is a valuable technique that helps engineers develop, validate, and optimize control algorithms and controllers cost-effectively, efficiently, and safely. It plays a crucial role in developing and deploying advanced engineering systems across various industries. In this paper, the researchers have confirmed the effectiveness of four phasor domain algorithms for rapidly securing power networks on control hardware setups. This is accomplished by employing the TMS320F28335 prototype in a hardware-in-the-loop configuration. The performance of these algorithms is evaluated on a real-time digital simulator (RTDS), using a simulated 9-bus system.

articleTitle: Speed Control of DC Motor Using Sliding Mode Controller Tuned by Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This research work investigates the effect of gain parameter tuning of the Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) using Genetic Algorithm (GA) on the speed control of the DC motor. The SMC tuned by GA shows a superior result compared to Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller and, the Ziegler-Nichols (ZN) tuning method. Rise time, settling time, and, percentage of overshoot was considered as the performance parameter of the DC motor. Integral time absolute error was used here as the objective function for tuning the gain parameters of SMC and PID controllers. The Lyapunov function ensured system stability in the case of SMC. The effect of variation of gain parameters of the sliding surface was also studied. The chattering effect was reduced by implementing a pseudo function. The whole work is carried out using the MATLAB Simulink platform.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Design and Performance Evaluation of Energy Generator Mechanical Rumble Strips
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)

authors.preferredName: A H M Khalid Reza Tonmoy

abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive design and demonstration of mechanical rumble strips aimed at generating energy from vehicles using their potential energy. The study addresses project sustainability and post-implementation facets. Mitigation strategies for these impacts are outlined, culminating in the refinement of technical specifications. The research evaluates solution and selects the "Rack Pinion Mechanism" as the best suitable choice. Creating detailed design, supported by 3D structural representations realized through "SOLIDWORKS." Employing "MATLAB" for necessary analysis and calculation. Also, design a complete electrical system to ensure operational safety. When a vehicle passes over the mechanical rumble strips it will press down and the kinetic energy will be converted into electrical energy with some mechanical and electrical equipment. To store the energy from the device, a battery pack will be connected through a charge controller and a DC-AC power inverter will be used. Every time a vehicle passes over the device, it produces energy and charges the battery. A prototype was created based on the design to conduct a comprehensive study and evaluation. A thorough performance evaluation was carried out which identified the design's limitations and areas that could be improved. Various loads were tested against the generator attached to the device to observe the load voltages and measure the total energy extracted from the system. The results were then compared against the estimations made earlier.

articleTitle: Web based-BigSync: A Grid Analytics Platform including Power System Database Management
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper discusses an offline engineering analytical software named BigSync (Big Data Analytics for Synchrophasors) developed at the Indian Institute of Technology, Palakkad. The software solution enables the user to perform offline engineering analysis by leveraging various power system measurements that are stored in a relational database (RDBMS). The software package includes applications such as data visualization, statistical analysis, data de-noising and anomaly detection/cyberattack detection. This paper details the applicability of the developed software product in the energy management system (EMS) or control room of a modern power system.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Home Monitoring and Danger Alert
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper describes an innovative IoT-driven home safety and automation system meant to create a safe and smart living environment. The system monitors possible household hazards by utilizing cutting-edge sensor technologies such as MQ2 gas and flame detectors and PIR motion sensors. Real-time messages and alerts are effortlessly provided to homeowners, regardless of their geographic location, via seamless Internet connectivity. Surprisingly, the system goes beyond simple notifications by utilizing responsive processes to manage threats like as gas leaks or flames on its own. This proactive strategy successfully stops harmful situations from worsening. The experimental findings demonstrate the system’s efficacy in real-world circumstances, emphasizing its accuracy, speed, and dependability. This work not only adds to improved home safety and security but also illustrates the potential of IoT-driven solutions in current residential environments. Future directions include improving sensor accuracy, expanding the system’s capabilities, and investigating advanced data analytics techniques to further enhance its performance.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Transient Stability for Coherent Generators in Multi-Machine Power Systems Using Static Var Compensator
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The uninterrupted supply of electric power is the lifeblood of modern society. The modern power system has more interconnections which makes it complex and vulnerable, in this context, the stability of multi-machine power systems takes on paramount importance. Within these intricate networks, coherent generators, operating in synchrony, can be particularly vulnerable to transient disturbances that threaten the reliable operation of the entire system. Static var compensators (SVCs), are a sophisticated and versatile technology designed to inject or absorb reactive power dynamically. SVCs, often considered the unsung heroes of power system control, emerge as a beacon of hope in the quest for enhanced transient stability. By skillfully adjusting voltage profiles and mitigating oscillatory behaviours, SVCs offer a compelling solution to the unique challenges posed by multi-machine power systems, especially those comprising coherent generators. This paper has shown the enhancement of transient stability for coherent generators by incorporating the SVC in the multi-machine power system. To achieve this goal SVC has been integrated into the IEEE 39 bus test power system and investigated the system thoroughly. The results of simulations that were provided in this paper show the addition of a static var compensator has helped to increase the transient stability of coherent generators.

articleTitle: SmartChargeNet: PCA-Enhanced Attention-LSTM for Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Wireless charging for electric vehicles (EVs) has gained significant popularity due to its contactless nature, eliminating the need for physical connections between the transmitter and receiver. This advancement in transportation contributes to environmental sustainability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, one of the key challenges in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems is the decrease in transmitted power and efficiency as the distance between the coils increases, resulting in power wastage. This paper focuses on the analysis of a WPT system designed for EV charging, taking into account various electrical and environmental factors to optimize the output power. The study explores how changes in the distance between adjacent coils impact the wireless power transfer process. Furthermore, the research involves data collection involving different shapes of transmitter and receiver coils, varying distances, and alignment scenarios. The proposed lightweight system, SmartChargeNet, is a novel system that uses a PCA-Enhanced Attention-LSTM network to predict received power in wireless EV charging systems. The system achieved an impressive R2 Score of 99.29%, demonstrating its effectiveness and accuracy using several metrics including Mean Squared Error (MSE), R2 Score, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE).

articleTitle: Revolution in Campus Transportation: The Autonomous Electric Vehicle With Smart Features
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Autonomous Electric Vehicle with RFID Card, a ground-breaking four-wheeled vehicle meant to transform campus transportation. Through sophisticated technology and environmentally sensitive engineering, this unique vehicle embodies the confluence of autonomy, sustainability, and passenger convenience. The system design incorporates an Arduino module, RFID card technology for exact student identification, sonar sensors for obstacle avoidance, and now, a GPS tracking device for expanded functionality. The vehicle’s engine features a BLDC motor controller, a 48-volt DC battery, and a 200 W solar panel for efficient and sustainable running. Its sturdy physical design includes a unique body composed of steel and iron, as well as a solar panel that charges the vehicle’s batteries. Precise steering, powered by a 300 KG ASME digital servo motor, assures passenger safety and comfort. Passengers may not only enjoy smooth RFID card-based identification but also trace their travel in real time with the inclusion of a GPS tracking device. This Autonomous Electric Vehicle promises to revolutionize campus mobility by providing excellent speed, efficiency, obstacle avoidance capabilities, and now accurate GPS-based monitoring for an all-encompassing transportation solution.

articleTitle: Short circuit performance of wind turbine generator step-up transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Wind turbine generators are becoming ubiquitous in India, adding to the renewable power generation. However, with a different topology compared to traditional generators, they bring a new set of transients to the grid. Every wind turbine generator will have an associated step-up transformer. Transformers have to withstand short circuit currents and they are generally tested for it. This paper presents a summary of the short circuit performance of wind turbine step-up transformers based on simulation and short circuit testing data.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Off-Grid Hybrid Power Plant with PV, Wind & Diesel Power for Uttar Char Fasson for Latest Data
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Bangladesh is currently facing a significant energy crisis, compounded by its limited foreign exchange reserves in the central bank. Despite being classified as a lower-middle-income country, the nation's electricity generation remains heavily reliant on non-renewable energy sources. This research seeks to address these pressing energy challenges by advocating for the adoption of renewable energy solutions. In response to these challenges, a tailored hybrid power plant model is presented for Uttar Char Fasson, an area often marginalized in energy discussions. Situated along the coast, Uttar Char Fasson boasts abundant solar radiation and wind potential, but it contends with erratic energy access. The model offers a practical solution to bridge this energy gap and reduce dependence on the central grid. The capabilities of HOMER Pro software are used to evaluate the viability and optimization of the suggested solution. Using real-time data, this software enables thorough simulations and analyses that cover costing, load demand, and energy production. The research findings demonstrate the practicality and significance of a tailored hybrid off-grid power system exclusively tailored for Uttar Char Fasson. This model effectively mitigates the energy crisis prevalent in underserved regions while simultaneously advancing environmental sustainability objectives. The primary contribution lies in harnessing the untapped potential of solar and wind energy sources, further enhanced by a robust battery storage mechanism.

articleTitle: Solar-powered IOT-Based Portable Refrigeration Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an IoT-based portable refrigeration unit, utilizing the Peltier effect for thermoelectric cooling. The design currently relies on conventional power sources, with potential future adaptations to incorporate solar energy, making it suitable for use in both remote and urban environments. The unit features an efficient dual Peltier element configuration within a heat chamber, ensuring rapid cooling. Moreover, the integration of IoT technology allows for real-time monitoring and control, enhancing its utility. The system’s performance was evaluated in various scenarios, confirming its potential as a solution for the preservation of food and pharmaceuticals in diverse settings. This study contributes to eco-friendly refrigeration methods, envisioning an alternative for communities with limited access to traditional cooling systems and highlighting the prospect of integrating solar energy in the future.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of GaAs, InAs and Silicon Nanowire by Using Modal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a modal analysis of GaAs, InAs and silicon nanowire to check their effective mode index. If the material refractive index of core is so high then light wave scattered, so don’t get the mode properly with the change of core radius. For medium refractive index of core, the electric and magnetic field of different x, y and z component intensity distribution of light wave gets properly. Here effective index curves measure the mode of those three materials with the help of increase of core radius. A modal analysis approach using finite Element methodology (FEM) employing a full-vectorial H-field formulation that has been customized to verify the single-mode operation.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impact of Various Stator Slot Configurations on Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are widely used for various industrial applications such as robotics, industrial drives, solar water pumping. Thus, a lot of research on the various performance of PMSM motors are ongoing. Some of the research includes rotor configuration, torque ripple, control techniques of PMSM and their magnetic design. The stator slot configuration has significant impact on the performance parameters of PMSM motors. Most importantly the torque profile and stator winding currents are highly influenced by the structure of stator slot. There are few research works are available in the exiting literatures which discuss about the impact of stator slot orientation on motor performances. In this paper, the impact of various stator slot configurations has been investigated on PMSM motors in terms of torque ripple profile, solid loss and stator winding current along with its total harmonic distortion (THD). Using the Ansys maxwell software package, a couple of 2D and 3D numerical models are designed and investigated by changing the stator slot geometry of PMSM motors, and the resultant torques and stator currents are recorded. This analysis could be a promising solution to the industrial engineers while selecting PMSM motors based on suitable stator slot geometry for specific industrial applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Energy Flow Strategy using Fuzzy-FOPI Controller for a Hybrid Energy Storage based Stand-alone DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Standalone microgrids utilize renewable energy sources with energy storage devices (ESDs) to supply high-quality power to the load. In this work, a stand-alone DC microgrid is considered, where solar PV is the primary source with battery, fuel cell and supercapacitor as ESDs. Unique characteristics of different ESDs are utilized together in the form of a hybrid energy storage system. It is challenging to distribute and balance the power among source, storage and load together. Therefore, an enhanced energy management system (EMS) for hybrid energy storage-based microgrids is presented with an effective controller to regulate the DC link voltage. A fuzzy-fractional order proportional integral (FOPI) controller is proposed, and a comparative analysis with FOPI and PI controllers is carried out to illustrate the significance of the proposed controller. The simulation study is carried out using the field data for solar irradiance and load profile as well.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of 4.8 kW Grid Connected Solar PV Based Water Pumping System for Sustainable Agricultural Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This research paper presents the modeling and simulation of 4.8 kW grid connected solar PV based water pumping system for sustainable agricultural irrigation. With a focus on reducing reliance on fossil fuels and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions, the proposed system integrates renewable energy solutions into agricultural practices. The core components, including the PV array, boost converter, and three-level voltage source converter (VSC), are carefully developed to optimize energy transfer and power generation. A maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is employed to extract the maximum power from the PV array, while smart control mechanisms ensure efficient power utilization and seamless grid integration. The simulated performance analysis under varying solar irradiance and temperature conditions demonstrates the system's robustness and effectiveness. The research aims to promote the adoption of renewable energy-based solutions in agriculture, fostering sustainable practices and contributing to a greener future for farming.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 21 level Symmetric Multilevel Inverter for Direct Grid Integration of Solar Photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A novel 21 level symmetric multilevel inverter topology with symmetric DC sources which is suitable for PV applications is proposed in this paper. The suggested 21-level multilevel inverter's design was created using MATLAB/Simulink and the effectiveness of the suggested topology has been assessed using a variety of load combinations including dynamic load fluctuations. Besides, the existing 21 level MLI topologies are compared to the suggested topology in terms of the quantity of switches, DC sources, diodes, capacitors, and gate driver circuits. The proposed topology exhibits satisfactory performance based on the points of comparison such as total devices count devices power rating, minimum blocking voltage and efficiency. Compared to Traditional topologies like NPC, DC, and CHB MLI. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the proposed topology is found 5.64% which is very close to IEEE standard.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of OFF-Grid Hybrid Energy System in Bangladesh Using HOMER
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The energy production of the future must be sustainable without harming human health or the environment. It seems impossible to satisfy the rising need for electricity with the current trends, creating scenarios for energy with reduced use of fossil fuels, nuclear energy, etc. In South Asia, Bangladesh is a developing nation with promising renewable energy sources. One of the country’s main problems is a severe energy crisis, such as the shortage of power generation for several decades. By implementing widespread utilization of renewable energy sources within the power sector, this problem can be alleviated. A hybrid renewable energy system is an ideal alternative to off-grid electrification of remote islands. Our objective is to develop an efficient hybrid energy system and conduct a thorough analysis of its technical and economic viability, optimization potential, sensitivity to variables, risk assessment and emission levels for the rural area of Bhola district known as Manpura using wind, PV, battery storage tank and natural gas generator by HOMER simulation software. An optimized hybrid system comprising PV, Wind Turbine, Battery, Converter, and Natural Gas Generator has been designed to fulfill the energy requirements of Manpura, an isolated rural community. The system will feed a daily load demand of 2733.44 kWh and a peak demand of 288.51 kW. Simulation results indicate a favorable Cost of Energy (COE) at $0.17/kWh and a Net Present Cost (NPC) totaling $4.23M.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Recent Power System Oscillations in North Eastern Region Grid of India
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: With the large-scale deployment of phasor measurement units, dynamic phenomena like low-frequency oscillations can be monitored in India. Low-frequency oscillation monitoring is required for the wide-area stability assessment in the power systems. The paper presents an investigation of oscillation events observed in the North Eastern Region grid of India. The paper provides a root cause analysis of the recent oscillation events by identifying the unstable oscillation-initiating node in the grid. Using archived event data. The investigation was carried out in two primary steps namely modal analysis and energy computation. It also highlights the reason behind the vulnerability of the North Eastern Region grid to increasing oscillations. The investigation is helpful to the system operator in pinpointing the unstable node in the grid.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Series Resistance Extraction Methods of Photovoltaic Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this study, five different methods from the literature, comprising both graphical and analytical methods, are used to determine the series resistance of ten different polycrystalline PV modules from three different manufacturers. The objective of this study is to understand how the different methods perform in terms of series resistance values. It is seen that graphical methods generate lower resistance values than analytical methods. However, all of the methods give a comparable pattern for the series resistances for the various modules. It represents that all methods are adequate for the comparative evaluation of polycrystalline-type modules. The third graphical technique, a comparison of the ideal and the series resistance-dependent non-ideal I-V curve, is preferred because it is easier to perform and provides resistance values from the maximum power point region of the I-V curve..

articleTitle: Sustainable University: On-Grid Solar PV Powered EVs Charging Station on Campus
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: It is frequently considered that universities are morally responsible for promoting sustainable practices, as they prepare a new generation of youth to take up work. An important step in promoting sustainability practices amongst university communities is to build a greener campus by means of sustainable transport infrastructure. The university can also support the transition towards zero transport carbon and UNs Sustainable Development Goals by sustainable electric vehicles (EVs). EVs can be charged using energy from fossil fuel or renewable energy resources. Fossil fuel based charging stations will still contribute to carbon emissions. Therefore, EV charging stations on campus must be powered by renewable energy sources to reduce carbon emissions. This paper aims to conduct a comparative economic and environmental analysis between standalone grid-powered and grid-connected solar PV powered EV charging stations at a university campus. Four types of energy system designs are considered: Grid only, Grid-Battery, PV-Grid and PV-Grid-Battery energy systems. Grid-Battery system is introduced here for charging batteries during off-peak hours and then discharging during peak hours which can reduce the electricity bill significantly. The net present cost, cost of electricity and carbon emission are used as performance indicators. The results show that the PV-Grid system is the best energy system among the four designs, in terms of economic and environmental benefits for EV charging stations.

articleTitle: Optimizing Photodegradation of Azo Dyes with Hydrothermal Synthesized ZnO Nanostructured Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Nanostructured ZnO thin films have been fabricated on the bared glass substrate using a simple, cost-effective, and uncovered hydrothermal method. It is observed that nanorods, nanotubes, nano-flux, hexagonal, and wurtzite structures have been grown uniformly. These thin films have been utilized as a photocatalyst to degrade azoic dyes from wastewater. This work aims to enhance the degradation rate without using a seed layer. The performance of photodegradation was observed by varying the molarity of zinc nitrate from 30 mM to 70 mM, keeping hexamethylene tetraamine (HMTA) constant at 50 mM. The maximum photodegradation efficiency was found for the thin film which was produced using 30 mM of Zn(NO3)2.6H2O. The efficiency was about 67.32%. The various properties of ZnO films fabricated at different concentrations of Zn(NO3)2.6H2O have been associated with the photodegradation performances of azoic dyes prepared by these ZnO films.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Transmission Line Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Unforeseen failures in the electrical power transmission line may arise due to various unpredictable factors. The occurrence of power failures on transmission lines has the potential to cause significant damage to the existing power grid unless prompt detection and correction of faults are carried out. The primary objective of this paper is to address the detection and classification of faults occurring on electrical power transmission lines. Specifically, the study focuses on a dataset consisting of 12,000 data points, each characterized by six distinct features. To achieve this, artificial neural networks are employed as the chosen methodology. The classification of transmission line faults was performed using various machine learning algorithms, including Linear Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, Random Forest, AdaBoost, Bagging Classifier, and XGBoost. The algorithms were evaluated based on parameters including accuracy, error rate, prediction speed, and training time. The findings suggest that tree-based classifiers have exhibited superior performance, achieving 100% accuracy in the classification of transmission line faults. On the other hand, Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machines (SVM) have yielded average results in this regard.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Power Monitoring and Management System of a Distribution Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Remote monitoring and control of a substation is a critical issue for the power or energy management department, which is typically done manually or with the help of a costly PLC and SCADA system. With the emergence of the internet and the computational era, a smart monitoring and trustworthy controlling system over the complete sub-station is extremely desirable, which may be accomplished by implementing Internet of Things (IoT) technology. A substation contains numerous electrical components such as transformers, breakers, relays, etc. The traditional method requires a regular manual testing system with limited precision. Furthermore, substations in metropolitan settings are more difficult to physically inspect, requiring more time to complete related tasks. In this research work a monitoring system has been proposed that is low-cost, user-friendly, and works automatically to avoid labor involvement and system loss. The results of the system are displayed in many ways to ensure that the system parameters will be monitored by more than one person for safety and protection reasons. A novel feature of automatic load management system is incorporated in this project which is absent in the latest work in the literature. When load demand is increased beyond the allocated power of a particular area a priority-based load shedding is performed automatically. The project is simulated using Proteus. Besides, a small prototype has been built to monitor physical operation. The uniqueness of this system is the display of results on desktop and mobile phones simultaneously.

articleTitle: Shared Encoder with Attention for Non-Intrusive Appliance Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) is a methodology used to deduce the power consumption and operational status of electrical equipment by analyzing the aggregated power signal of a residential or commercial structure. Utilizing detailed electric load profiles obtained from smart meters has generated growing interest in employing this method for demand-side energy management within smart grids. NILM is a time series regression problem that involves appliance state classification, pattern recognition, and anomaly detection. Deep learning-based NILM techniques have shown promising results, but they are often applicable to a limited number of appliances due to their complex model architecture and huge computational cost. This paper proposes an improved method by using a shared convolutional encoder architecture for a multitask decoder network, adding multi-head attention blocks in between. The proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in the publicly available REDD data set while requiring a reduced amount of training time.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Consumer Power Management: Unveiling Power Grid Feasibility Analysis Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: As distributed energy sources become more prevalent, maintaining power grid stability is increasingly challenging. By integrating machine intelligence and communication technologies, traditional power networks could transform into smart grids. Through machine learning and artificial intelligence, these smart grids can adeptly respond to unexpected changes in consumer demand, power interruptions, surges in renewable energy production, and other crucial situations. Variations in power generation and loads, along with changes in the power system’s structure, lead to varying shifts in the entire network’s active power. Detecting these fluctuations through manual analysis is laborious, but machine learning can be highly impactful in this regard. This study aims to collect comprehensive data for analyzing grid stability, utilizing machine learning tools to thoroughly examine the data, and adopting a multimodal approach to compare model outcomes for an improved solution strategy. Our analysis reveals an accuracy exceeding 0.97, indicating strong potential for practical application and implications.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study of Small Hydroelectric Power Plant at Madhabkunda Waterfall, Moulvibazar, Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Electricity generation from hydropower is generally regarded as a cost-effective energy option. In this article, the potential for the construction of a small hydropower station at the Madhabkunda waterfall, situated in the Barlekha Upazila of the Moulvibazar district of Bangladesh, is examined. The primary objective of this study was to determine the potential electricity generation capacity that could be attained by the establishment of a small hydroelectric power station at the Madhabkunda waterfall. The flow rate, resulting in the output power, is determined by employing a pitot tube. Furthermore, a reservoir design is proposed as a means of mitigating flow fluctuations. It is indicated by our research that the Madhabkunda waterfall possesses a sufficient head and an available flow rate conducive to the support of a small hydroelectric power facility. The results demonstrate that small hydropower at Madhabkunda has the capacity to provide a monthly average power output ranging from 1.74 MW to 2.56 MW during the rainy season months.

articleTitle: Third Order Integral Terminal Sliding Control for DC-DC Converter Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In DC bus, constant power loads (CPLs) are connected in DC distribution networks (DCDNs) which causes the system instability due to the negative impedance properties of CPLs. To ensure system stability, a third-order integral terminal sliding mode controller (3-ITSMC) is proposed using an improved quick-reaching law. In this proposed control scheme, an improved reaching law is used to mitigate chattering from the system and tackles the underlying issue of the non-minimum phase in DC-DC boost converters (DDBCs). Through the Lyapunov stability theory, 3-ITSMC controller can ensure the stability of the entire system which is the main aim of this proposed 3-ITSMC. The performance of the proposed control scheme is validated through the simulation investigations implemented in MATLAB/Simulink under major fluctuations demonstrating that it enhances the stability of DCDNs in every aspect as compared to the existing sliding mode controllers. After the simulation, the tracking error of 3-ITSMC is 20% for DC voltage variation. Additionally, for the variations in CPLs’ power, the tracking error of 3-ITSMC is 18%.

Author Keywords: third-order integral terminal sliding mode controller

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Time Scheduled Automatic Cleaning System of Dust Accumulation for Optimizing Solar Power Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems have emerged as a dependable and commercially accepted source of renewable energy since 1995. However, several factors significantly affect the efficiency of PV modules in harnessing solar energy. Among these factors, dust accumulation stands out as a primary element that diminishes efficiency and increases deterioration rates over time. To maximize the output power of PV systems, this research introduces an innovative automatic solar PV cleaning system. This system employs an Aluminum alloy-based mechanical design and integrates a time-scheduled controlling unit. Through experimental implementation, the developed prototype has demonstrated the potential to enhance the generated output power by approximately 10–15%. This remarkable increase in efficiency represents a significant step towards optimizing solar power production and ensures a cleaner and more sustainable energy source for the future.

articleTitle: Energy Management System of a PV-Based Grid-Connected Electric Vehicle in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A growing percentage of the transportation demand is being met by internal combustion vehicles powered by fossil fuels, which has a detrimental effect on the environment. As electric vehicles (EVs) are free from toxic gases and are easy on passengers, they’re becoming increasingly popular. However, these EVs have a negative impact on the grid. Consequently, there is an immense demand for a charging station powered by renewable energy. In this study, a grid-connected, solar photovoltaic (PV) array-powered, residential EV charger that serves the needs of EVs, DC load, and the grid is proposed in the context of Bangladesh. Here we’ve implemented an existing modified perturb and observe algorithm. A technique for energy management based on DC-link voltage regulation has been used. The method was validated using MATLAB/SIMULINK. In islanded mode, the PV array produced power is distributed among the load and EV battery. The EV drains to meet the load demand if the PV array power is inadequate, and the EV battery charges if the PV array power is adequate. However, the grid-connected mode is active if the PV power is not there. According to the need, the EV can function in both G2V (Grid to Vehicle) and V2G (Vehicle to Grid) modes. The charger is additionally actively filtered to maintain the grid current’s total harmonic distortion below 5%.

articleTitle: A Thorough Probe into Enhancing Energy Harvesting via Piezo-Modules in Metrorail Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In the current global focus on sustainable and eco-friendly energy sources, energy harvesting has emerged as a significant area of interest. This research provides a detailed explanation of the design process for an energy harvesting prototype with piezo electric modules and the power conditioning circuit employed to optimize energy capture. The study primarily aims to explore efficient energy generation and capture methods. The electric energy generated by these modules through direct strain or ambient vibration is influenced by factors such as the number of piezoelectric transducers, the harvesting circuit, applied load, and arrangement scheme. The design and testing of the model were intended for scalability and increased power generation. This research assesses the effectiveness of various piezoelectric module connections for power generation in the 17-station of MRT line-6 project of Bangladesh. It comprehensively explores the performance of piezoelectric modules in different configurations like series, parallel, and series-parallel combined. Results show significant potential in these combinations, producing impressive power outputs under an average 60kg pressure: 0.1674mW, 0.242mW, and 0.2223mW for series, parallel, and series-parallel setups, respectively. Rigorous data analysis leads to the clear conclusion of outstanding performance. These findings are crucial for understanding the use of piezoelectric modules in generating power for transportation systems and suggest opportunities for further research in this domain.

articleTitle: Automated Trash Collector and Composting Robot Design for IoT-based Climate Friendly Recycling
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Automated Trash Collector and Composting Robot performs the building-to-building trash collection with a built-in climate friendly electric composter that helps to recycle the wastage in an environment friendly way. A significant amount of recycling through this, will also assist the bio-mass power generation process over the time. It is designed to collect trash under a star network from every house and can travel to the right destination using its radar or lidar to overcome the obstacles. The trash bot utilizes solar power to charge it up for daily process. Star system network can be assigned to each robot to perform the control and automation segments of it. The standard design of this paper is being presented as a part of solution for upcoming climate issues, which can reduce a significant part of daily urban pollution.

articleTitle: A Heuristic Approach for Resolution of Issues in Power System Applications in SCADA/ EMS System at National Load Despatch Centre
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition & Energy Management Systems (SCADA/EMS) System are extensively used at load despatch Centres worldwide for real time grid operation in Power System. These systems are equipped with several Power System applications (PSA) features as required for operators to make informed decisions. These applications are generic to a great extent and are part of the overall functionality of the SCADA/EMS system. State Estimation (SE), Contingency Analysis (CA), Optimal power flow (OPF), etc. are some of the widely and commonly used applications in SCADA/EMS system. The smooth running of these applications is of prime importance to ensure safe and economic grid operation. Besides providing situational awareness to system operators it also gives meaningful full information about violations, vulnerabilities and operational issues which may result in potential problems in real time grid operation. Solution and results obtained from these applications primarily depends on SCADA data and correct modeling of the power system network. The source of SCADA data may be directly reporting from sub stations or from other control Centres through Inter Control Centre Protocol (ICCP) data. Further regular tuning of key parameters also plays an important role in the successful running of PSA application. This paper provides the issues and their mitigation in heuristic manner which are encountered during the running of these applications at national level i.e. National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) in India.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement of Grid Connected Wind Generation System Using FACTS Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The variable nature of wind resources, coupled with the dynamic behavior of wind power conversion systems, often lead to fluctuations and disturbances in the electrical grid, impacting power quality and stability. Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS) devices emerges as a cutting-edge solution to enhance power quality and optimize the integration of wind energy into the grid. This paper proposes a technique for improving power quality in grid-connected wind power conversion systems through the deployment of FACTS devices. A Proportional-Integral (PI) controlled Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) is employed with the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) based wind energy conversion system (WECS) feeding a nonlinear load and the grid. The integrated WECS-FACTS system is implemented in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment to assess its performance under various loading conditions. Extensive simulation studies demonstrated that the suggested technique successfully reduced the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the main current from 27.67% to 4.28%. This significant improvement in power quality suggests that the proposed technique can be considered as a viable solution for THD reduction in both stand-alone and grid-connected WECS.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Topologies of Grid-Tied Photovoltaic Generation with PWM Power Factor Corrector
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: To reduce the emissions of polluting gases and fulfill the increasing demand for electricity, a green energy source like the Photovoltaic (PV) system is getting more popular. In this work, the modeling and control of single-stage and two-stage grid-connected photovoltaic systems based on perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm with grid-connected power factor corrector (PFC) followed by a DC load are carried out using MATLAB/Simulink. The maximum power is extracted from the PV array under varying environmental conditions using a conventional P&O algorithm. Though both topologies intelligently track the maximum power, single-stage topology shows better performance. However, two-stage topology provides more consistent DC output voltage than single-stage topology. Since DC loads have become ubiquitous in every human’s life, a grid-connected DC load is further analyzed here. When the DC load is connected via an uncontrolled rectifier, the grid current becomes distorted and the system power factor reduces. So, a PWM rectifier has been chosen which makes the system almost unity power factor and keeps the harmonic content within the allowable range of 2.54%.

articleTitle: Revisiting Power Swing Blocking Schemes for Future Power Systems with High Penetration of Inverter Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The deployment of large-scale renewable energy sources as a part of the transformation to green energy has led to significant changes in the control and operation of power system networks. Renewable energy sources (RES) like solar PV arrays and wind turbines are connected to the power grid through power electronics converters, which do not inherently contribute to system inertia and result in the reduction of total inertia in the power system to a greater extent. In this paper, we review the effect of penetration of inverter-based resources (IBR) on the legacy power swing blocking (PSB) schemes. A mathematical analysis is done to find the relationship between system inertia using the inertia distribution index (IDI) and the rate of change of impedance (ROCI) at the relay locations. Dynamic simulation is performed on the IEEE-9 Bus system to evaluate the performance of traditional PSB schemes in the presence of IBR. The results indicate that the setting of conventional PSB schemes will be more difficult in the presence of high IBR penetration. Furthermore, a possible way to identify vulnerable PSB relays is investigated based on the correlation information between IDI and ROCI.

articleTitle: An Optimal Load Scheduling Approach for Residential Energy Consumers of Bangladesh based on Time of Use Tariff Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The rapid growth of urbanization and increasing energy demand in Bangladesh have posed significant challenges for maintaining a reliable and sustainable power supply. This study contributes to the development of a practical and efficient load scheduling approach for residential energy consumers in Bangladesh. In order to reduce electricity costs and flatten the load curve, appliances are categorized and shifted from busy hours to off-peak hours through the process of load scheduling. Time-varying tariff schemes are uncommon in our country, but by charging more during peak hours and encouraging users to alter their consumption patterns, they help to lower demand. For our work, Time of Use (TOU) tariff rate was chosen. The objective was to develop an efficient scheduling algorithm that minimizes electricity costs while considering consumer comfort and the constraints imposed by the TOU pricing structure. Firstly, a load profile was created by gathering data from residential areas. Then an objective function was developed to minimize electricity costs and find optimal scheduling that maintains user comfort as well as reduces Peak-to-Average Ratio (PAR). The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm was then applied to solve the optimization problem, aiming to minimize the total electricity cost while satisfying comfort and convenience constraints. MATLAB was used to simulate the PSO algorithm and evaluate its performance in generating optimal load schedules for residential energy consumers. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing electricity costs by 14% for consumers while considering their comfort requirements and keeping the schedule within two hours of the original consumption time. Also, a reduction in loads during peak hours by shifting them to off-peak hours is also observed.

articleTitle: A Robust PI-Type-II Compensator for DC-DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: DC-DC converters are extensively utilized in switch-mode regulated power supplies, renewable energy conversion systems, and electrical drives. Various controllers have already been employed for the regulation of its output voltage. However, these controllers provide poor tracking performance, increased steady-state errors (SSE), and reduced stability. In this work, the integration of a proportional integral (PI) controller with a type-II compensator is proposed to enhance the boost converter's performance. The average state space modeling technique is used for the boost converter. The compensator design and analysis are done using the k-factor approach. The PI controller minimizes SSEs, while the type-II compensator provides maximum phase boost to enhance transient response and stability. Combining the PI and type-II compensator in parallel increases the phase margin (PM), ensuring stable converter operation. The proposed compensator's performance has been thoroughly evaluated using the MATLAB/Simulink platform and laboratory experiments, encompassing load variation and comparing it against various controllers. This comprehensive testing affirms that the proposed compensator surpasses the performance of alternative controllers, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: IoT-based Energy Optimization and Demand Response System for Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into the existing power system creates opportunities and problems for energy optimization and demand response. This project presents an IoT-based energy optimization and demand response system for successfully harnessing renewable energy and optimizing energy usage. The system employs a network of sensors and actuators to collect real-time data on energy consumption, environmental conditions, and renewable energy output. This data is processed and analyzed with energy optimization algorithms to find potential for energy savings and demand response solutions. The system offers intelligent control of energy-consuming devices using optimization algorithms, aiding load balancing, demand forecasting, and peak shaving. Additionally, it integrates demand response techniques such as load shedding and load shifting to adapt energy consumption to grid circumstances and maximize the utilization of renewable energy sources. The system includes wireless communication modules for IoT connectivity, enabling remote monitoring, control, and data sharing with a central server or cloud platform.

articleTitle: A High Performing Approach to Short-Term PV Power Forecasting using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The use of solar energy has been gaining popularity around the world as a clean and sustainable source of energy. However, the variability of solar power generation due to weather patterns poses challenges for integrating solar power into the grid and ensuring a reliable energy supply. To address these challenges, short-term solar photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting using machine learning (ML) algorithms has emerged as a promising solution. This study investigates the effectiveness of different ML algorithms for short-term PV power forecasting, provides an overview of factors affecting the performance with time-series based data, and proposes high performance approaches. Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-term Memory (LSTM), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms have been examined on a one-year dataset of 88,494 with 20 features and 15-min resolution. Root means square error (RMSE) and mean square error (MSE) are considered as the accuracy measure and found that both ANNs and LSTM outperform SVM. A thorough comparison with recently published results shows the superiority of the proposed approaches. This success of ANNs and LSTM can be attributed to their ability to capture the complex and non-linear relationships present in the data. SVMs are more suited to handle linear relationships and may struggle with the complexities of short-term solar power forecasting. Although more research is needed to generalize this observation, these findings will serve as a valuable guide who wish to work in the area of PV power forecasting.

articleTitle: A Current Based Sampling Controlled Fractional Open Circuit Voltage MPPT Method for PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A conventional fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is a simple and fast technique to get maximum power from a photovoltaic (PV) panel. The major drawback of the technique is that the PV panel is detached from the load periodically for sampling the open circuit voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf> which causes loss of power. Since a frequent disconnection of the load from the panel is to be avoided, the sampling rate of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf> must be kept as low as possible. If the sampling rate is kept too small, there will be a significant power loss, because the PV panel output power follows a fixed reference during one sampling interval. If the solar irradiance changes within the sampling interval, a new MPP won't be traced until the succeeding sampling interval starts. This paper proposes a current based sampling controlled FOCV method which has no such dilemma. The proposed MPPT method has no fixed sampling rate, and it samples V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf> only when there is an environmental change. It is shown that the proposed method tracks the MPP more accurately than the conventional one, and thus the dynamic efficiency of the system increases by 6.17%.

articleTitle: Shadow Length Impact on Inter-Row Spacing: Investigation for Agrivoltaic in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This study analyzes the impact of shadow length on the panel inter row spacing for a particular prospective agricultural field at Rangpur District situated in the northern part of Bangladesh. The objective is to calculate the optimum inter-row spacing for that field. Result shows that to get maximum energy throughout the year the tilt angle of the panels should be equal to latitude which is 25.67 degree for the studied site, and the shadow length due to this angle during noon time is taken as the optimum inter-row distance which is 0.5 meter.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor Estimation Based on Modified Demodulation-Cascaded Delayed Signal Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Synchrophasors are a cutting-edge wide-area power system monitoring and control technologies, particularly for contemporary networks with a significant renewable energy component. Two reference synchrophasor models are suggested in the IEEE/IEC 60255-118-1 standard for the building of synchrophasor units for protection (P-class) and measuring (M-class) applications. In this paper, an improved P-class synchrophasor technique based on modified demodulation is proposed. A frequency adaptable second harmonic oscillator is incorporated at the traditional modulation approach to dampen high amplitude oscillations that result from it. A low pass filter based on delayed signal cancellation (DSC), which is computationally effective and highly capable of extracting selected harmonic is utilized to enhance the performance of estimates in challenging circumstances. Results indicate that the proposed synchrophasor model significantly improves steady state compliance while simultaneously reducing the dynamic error margin.

Author Keywords: Rate of change of frequency error(RFE)

articleTitle: An Integrated Approach for Fault Detection, Classification and Location in Solar PV Array
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: World is adapting sustainable energy solutions to the mainstream power grid and solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation is becoming one of the most prominent sources of energy. The generation of solar PV energy is entirely dependent on climate and weather conditions. Often, a solar PV plant is exposed to extreme environmental conditions. These conditions can result in a variety of faults that can disrupt their energy yield. This paper proposes an integrated approach for detecting electrical faults in solar PV plants in real time onload condition, classifying those faults, and precisely locating the faulty PV panel. The proposed method is tested using field data for faults like open circuit, short circuit as well as partial shading and degradation. The proposed approach is integrated and uses the trained ANN model based on field data. This makes the proposed method accurate and precise as well as appropriate for IoT-based applications.

articleTitle: An Inverter Control Agnostic Fault Detection Solution based on the Dynamic Time Warping Philosophy
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Deployment of inverter-interfaced renewable energy resources (IIRERs) in power systems has put a question mark on reliability of existing line protection schemes. Despite great economic and environmental benefits of IIRERs, the unpredictable fault behavior of IIRERs due to various inverter control philosophies makes the existing line protection schemes vulnerable to maloperations. This paper proposes a new local voltage information based fault detection scheme deployed using dynamic time warping technique, that is agnostic to controls implemented by neighbouring IIRERs. The proposed scheme is validated on CIGRE 14-bus system and IEEE 9 Bus system in the presence and absence of grid code for both operational and fault events. The results demonstrate reliable operation of the proposed fault detection scheme in the presence of IIRERs.

articleTitle: Integrated Measurement and Model Based Fast Small Signal Stability Assessment for Renewable Integrated Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Increased penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) into the power grid will change the dynamic behavior of the system which was earlier dominated by synchronous generators. A detailed study on the impact of Type-IV wind turbine generators (WTG) on the inter-area mode is carried out in this paper. The frequency of oscillation (FOO) and the corresponding damping of inter-area mode for different tie-line power is analyzed. Fast-Small Signal Stability Assessment(Fast-SSSA) application, a hybrid method that utilizes both measurements as well as model-based inputs is proposed for stability assessment considering the damping limit of inter-area mode. The practical implementation of the proposed method for control room application is detailed. The suggested methodology provides a faster and more accurate stability assessment software solution for the control room application.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Efficacy of Differential Relay Systems for Transformer Protection Under Different Internal Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Transformers play a crucial role in the electric power system, and it is essential to protect them adequately. To address the risk of transformer damage during faults, faster and more selective protection measures are required. In this study, the performance of a differential relay was successfully simulated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform. The data found from the proposed model were used to train an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to predict the relay tripping. The main objective was to investigate the protection of power transformer from internal faults and prevent any interference with the power system. Several plausible fault scenarios were evaluated. It was thoroughly examined how the relays performed under different system characteristics and fault conditions. Additionally, the ANN model was successfully trained to predict the differential relay tripping under different fault scenarios and locations.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Perovskite Based Solar Cells Without and With Different ETM/HTM Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Perovskite solar cell technology is an advanced solar cell which is becoming popular day by day for its good performance. In basic perovskite solar cell structure Electron Transport Material (ETM) and Hole Transport Material (HTM) plays an important role in overall efficiency. In this paper, the performance of perovskite solar cell model has been studied with and without different ETM and HTM layers. Without ETM and HTM layers, the highest power conversion efficiency has been found for an 18×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>m thick perovskite material 24.16% out of 14 different perovskite material thickness. 11 types of combination of different materials have been used for ETM and HTM layers. Out of 11 ETM-HTM layer combinations, the use of MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as ETM layer of 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>m thickness, ZnO_aunr_China as HTM layer of 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>m thickness and absorber layer Perovskite 25×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>m of has showed a best efficiency of 27.69%.

articleTitle: System Strength Impact Assessment of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
