abstract: This paper presents an assessment of system strength by analyzing the available fault level (AFL) and the variations in AFL with increasing penetration factors for three different generations: asynchronous generation (AG) e.g., induction generator, inverter-based generation (IBG) e.g., photovoltaic, and battery storage system (BSS). System strength in the power system is analyzed considering faults at a particular location. The effects of system strength are evaluated considering Tasmanian power system and IEEE 14 BUS system. The integration of AG reduces system strength, while the other two generations have a negligible impact on system strength. Hence, it is crucial to address the AG integration issues for ensuring system stability. This research also aims to conduct dynamic simulations of these systems to analyze stability and mitigate risks. Incorporating the static condenser (STATCON) improves the strength and stability of the system and mitigates the risks. PSS®E Xplore 34.0 software platform is used for all the simulation purposes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Chemical Process for Crystalline Solar Cell Recycling: A State of the art Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The increasing adoption of crystalline silicon solar cells as a renewable energy solution has led to a growing concern regarding the proper management of end-of-life photovoltaic modules. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of chemical processes for the recycling of crystalline solar cells, focusing on state-of-the-art technologies. The recycling of crystalline silicon cells by the chemical process where we identified that the chemical process for extracting silicon from PV modules is considerably more effective than all other techniques and technologies. A comparative analysis is made from all the chemical processes containing chemical compositions with a greater extraction of silicon. The results show that the significance of the chemical processes not only depends on the chemical element but also depends on the temperature. Besides a comprehensive assessment is done to address the growing challenges associated with end-of-life solar modules.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Single-Phase Inverter Topology by Using Modified Triangular Carrier Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The demand for electrical power has risen day by day in the present period. The inverter is used to transform power from DC to AC. By using DC to AC conversion topologies, a decreased switch inverter is the best option for this energy conversion due to its advantages such as low cost, better output power, lower switching loss, lesser third harmonic distortion, and lower electromagnetic interference. But it also has a downside, including more switching devices needed for higher levels, huge size, and high cost. This paper mainly suggested that only four switches, one voltage source for generating voltage waveforms, belong to a newly invented topology with a decreased THD. Different types of pulse width modulation techniques are used to decrease the harmonic variable or total harmonic distortion, including trapezoidal triangular carrier SPWM with better output with low THD. This proposed inverter's key benefit ends in decreased capacity along with low installation costs and is ideal for power applications. The proposed inverter was simulated through the software of MATLAB Simulink. The total harmonic distortion of the proposed inverter is 43.61% using the trapezoidal triangular carrier SPWM modulation technique when the carrier frequency is 2000 Hz and the modulation index is 1. The THD is less when the carrier frequency is 2000 Hz and the THD is 43.82%.

articleTitle: Determination of Optimal Locations for Installation of Solar Photovoltaic Farm in Maharashtra, India
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: For efficient utilisation of renewable energy sources, it is crucial to determine the geographical locations where these sources are abundantly available. In India, the state of Maharashtra is one of most prominent sources of solar energy. This paper presents an assessment of location suitability for installation of solar PV farms across various districts in Maharashtra.The solar PV output depends on multiple factors such as solar irradiation, air temperature, slope of the land etc. In addition, the optimality of a site also depends on geographical factors like the presence of archaeological sites, disaster-prone nature of the land and land cover. Each of these factors influences the decision of site selection. The degree by which each of these factors affects the decision, known as the criteria weight is evaluated using Analytical Hierarchy Process. The distribution maps of the considered factors are scaled by their criteria weights using Quantum Geographic Information System. These maps are then overlaid on the map of Maharashtra to obtain a resultant map depicting the most suitable sites for solar farm installation.

articleTitle: Towards Carbon-Neutral Healthcare Facilities: Design and Evaluation of a Renewable Energy Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) demand clean and reliable energy delivery. Here, we present a comprehensive study focusing on the design, analysis, and social impact assessment of a microgrid system tailored for a hospital. The microgrid is designed to support both grid-connected and islanded operation modes, incorporating PV panels, wind turbines, combined heat and power (CHP) systems, and energy storage. In this case study, our objective was to ensure an uninterrupted power supply during grid blackouts, achieving a minimum of 75% electricity demand coverage for at least 5 consecutive days. A detailed cost analysis is conducted, considering alternative design configurations and the influence of discount rates on the economic feasibility of the system. To promote environmental sustainability, a constraint is imposed on carbon emissions, aiming to keep them below 50% of the grid emissions. Additionally, a comprehensive social impact assessment is performed to evaluate the effects of the proposed microgrid project on various stakeholders in the surrounding area. The integrated approach of renewable energy integration, cost analysis, environmental constraints, and social impact assessment contributes to a holistic evaluation, enabling the successful implementation of microgrid systems in similar contexts.

articleTitle: A Fast Response Fault Detection Technique for HVAC Transmission Line Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: High voltage alternating current (HVAC) transmission lines are the only way to transmit electrical energy from the power plant to the utilities. There are several types of transmission line faults that can interrupt the power supply, sometimes even resulting in national blackout. To ensure a highly reliable power supply system, detecting the faults in the quickest of time is crucial. This research used machine learning and neural network algorithm to find five different types of faults using data from a real power transmission line in Bangladesh. Apart from the accuracy of the methods, the focus was given on the response time in identifying the faults. The two boosting methods CatBoost and XGBoost stood out as the most precise among all the algorithms, achieving excellent accuracy and detection time in between 20 ms to 30 ms. The response time of all the methods was found to be in millisecond range, making them perfect for not only long term faults, but also to be implied in transient fault analysis.

articleTitle: Moisture Withstand Capability of Natural Ester Based Dielectric Oils for Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Power transformer, being one of the most essential components of electrical power network, facilitates the transmission and distribution of electricity. Dielectric oil is one of the key factors for the reliable operation of power transformers. For the excellent cooling capability and great insulation, mineral oil (MO) has been used in the power transformers as a dielectric oil for over a century. However, being a non-biodegradable liquid, discovery of biodegradable dielectric oil is on its way. Natural ester based dielectric oils proved its worthiness to replace mineral oil (MO) in past research. If a transformer is refilled with natural ester based dielectric oil, it is likely that 20% of the mineral oil (MO) residue will still be present. Mixtures of 80% natural ester + 20% mineral oil (MO) are also investigated in terms of dielectric breakdown voltage, viscosity, moisture content, etc. However, investigations on the moisture withstand capability of these mixtures are scarce. In this paper, investigation of the moisture withstand capability of three natural esters i.e., soybean oil (SO), palm oil (PO) and mustard oil (MUO) mixed with mineral oil (MO) is done. The comparison of these mixed oils with non-mixed oil in terms of dielectric breakdown voltage is also shown when no moisture is added. It is hoped that the results of this experiment will fill a gap of using natural ester based dielectric oils in power transformer.

articleTitle: Assessing the Techno-Economic Feasibility of Cogeneration Systems in Bangladesh’s Sugar Mills
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This study addresses Bangladesh’s persistent energy deficit by proposing an innovative solution: small-scale cogeneration plants in sugar mills. Leveraging bagasse and biogas, the research estimates their potential for electricity generation, considering both seasonal variations and limitations. Economic feasibility is evaluated through cost analysis and break-even point determination. Environmental feasibility is assessed in terms of carbon dioxide generation. Results demonstrate significant electricity generation potential of 42.01 MW in-season and 68.98 MW off-season, capable of supplementing the national grid. This eco-friendly cogeneration system enhances sugar mills’ financial viability and contributes to Bangladesh’s power stability. The application of this study to North Bengal Sugar Mills showcases a promising 6.5 MW electricity generation capacity. The research advocates a profitable and sustainable future for Bangladesh’s sugar industry, offering valuable insights for energy-deficient regions globally.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Placement of Battery Energy Storage Systems for Enhancement of Grid Frequency Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In recent times, the integration of renewable energy sources has led to the displacement of traditional inertia-based generating stations which can lead to the degradation of the frequency stability of power systems. This study proposes a method to enhance the system frequency stability by formulating an optimization problem. The objective of the proposed method is to maximize the system frequency nadir with the constraints being the optimum size and location of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs). The proposed method is then solved using three swarm-based metaheuristic optimization algorithms: Bat Algorithm (BA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Firefly Algorithm (FA), and is tested in the IEEE 9-bus system. Upon integration of BESS at the proposed locations, the frequency nadir was improved by 2.0104 Hz and 4.4557 Hz for the outages of the largest and second-largest generators, respectively. Additionally, the obtained results show that the proposed method provides a better frequency enhancement than the compared method.

articleTitle: Optimal Solar Array Configuration for Multiple Shade Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The Renewable Energy Sources (RES) participating in the stable and reliable grid operation is increasing exponentially. Solar PV has a major contribution to the increased grid integration of RES. Optimal output should be obtained from the connected solar PV arrays. These arrays are connected in series and parallel to operate at Maximum Power Point (MPP) under normal conditions. However, under partially shaded conditions, some panels may be shaded, and the output of the whole array may not be optimized. Switching of panels is utilized to obtain maximum output in such conditions. In this paper, multiple metaheuristic methods like Particle Swarm Optimization, Manta Ray Foraging Optimization, Gorilla Troop Optimizer, and Bald Eagle Search are employed to obtain the optimal solar array configuration in multiple shaded patterns for a 9 × 9 array. These configurations are obtained under individual shading patterns, and multiple shaded patterns are considered simultaneously. MATLAB is used for implementing the metaheuristic techniques.

articleTitle: LQR Based Current Controller for Improved Power Quality of Grid-Tied PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new LQR-based feedforward current control scheme for the three-phase inverter of a grid-tied PV system to achieve better power quality. In order to mitigate the THD in the grid current and variation in the grid voltage, the proposed control mechanism combines an LQR-based feedforward current regulator with a disturbance decoupling approach. The feedback gains of the current regulator are obtained using the LQR method and the fluctuation in the grid voltage is modeled as a disturbance to get rid of its effect. In order to mitigate the computational complexity, the control strategy is developed in the synchronous reference frame (SRF) and to verify its effectiveness, the PV system along with the controller is simulated under various operating situations using the Matlab/Simulink platform. The simulation results show that the proposed LQR-based current control scheme has been more successful in improving the power quality of grid-tied PV systems than some of the conventional controllers, particularly in decreasing the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in the grid current.

articleTitle: Optimizing Emergency Lamp Drivers: A Focus on the Developing World Context
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized driver system designed for emergency self-ballasted lamps, with a Battery Management System (BMS) and intelligent power failure detection. The system is specifically tailored to address the challenges inherent in Bangladesh's power infrastructure, which is marked by recurrent outages and voltage fluctuations. The aims of the proposed driver system include minimization of energy consumption, improvement of battery management, and the implementation of intelligent power failure detection, ensuring continuous illumination. In order to accomplish this, a power-failure detection circuit and a protection IC are used. The presented system demonstrates notable attributes, including a high-efficiency level of 72.5%, a reduced battery charging duration of 240 minutes, an extended backup duration of 180 minutes, and adept power failure detection and adaptation to varying voltage ranges for illumination and battery charging. Consequently, this research presents a promising solution to address the distinctive lighting challenges prevalent in Bangladesh, aligning with the nation's energy goals.

articleTitle: LVRT Capability Enhancement of Doubly-Fed Induction Generator using Multi-Stage Control
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Modern power system needs a stable wind farm operation during and after the fault as per the grid code. The doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based energy conversion systems are the most popular among wind turbine technologies. However, the DFIG-based wind farms require complete low voltage ride through (LVRT) and reactive power control to meet the grid code. This paper proposes a multi-stage control (MSC) that enhances the LVRT and reactive current injection capability of DFIG. The proposed MSC algorithm includes three stages: stage 1, stage 2, and stage 3. Stage 1 and Stage 2 are responsible for the improved LVRT control, and stage 3 for the system’s recovery. The presented methodology aids the LVRT using the existing protection circuit (crowbar and DC link chopper) and modified electromagnetic torque-based inner control. The proposed algorithm is validated on the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) platform.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Compensation Studies With Variable Shunt Reactor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Reactive power compensation for system planning in IEEE bus systems is presented in this paper. In this paper, overload control for transmission lines, simulation of the IEEE 30,118 bus system, and contingency analysis are presented. Power flow correctional devices known as Variable Shunt Reactors (VSR) are essential for managing reactive power flow and loading in lines. A discussion is given to the best location and application of VSR to control power flow and regulate the lines connecting to the 138 kV and 345 kV voltage levels of the bus systems. Reactive power compensation in the system is investigated through the application of the VSR research. The results of the simulation are verified by the software Dig-SILENT Power Factory.

articleTitle: Virtual power plants and net zero targets: A case study of the United Kingdom
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: With increasing international climate concerns, getting to net zero emissions has become a top priority for many countries. The energy sector is crucial to the shift to a future powered by sustainable energy. To this end, virtual power plants (VPPs), have emerged as a powerful tool with the ability to transform energy systems by integrating renewable energy sources (RES), energy storage technologies, enabling demand response programs, empowering consumer participation, and improving grid management. This study presents a detailed analysis of VPPs as a way of achieving net-zero targets, focusing on the case study of the United Kingdom (UK). By assessing the UK's energy environment, its energy policies and legislative framework, the advancement of renewable energy technologies, increasing flexibility, and the transition towards sustainable energy systems. The approach presented shows the viability of VPPs to lower carbon footprint and emphasizes on accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels to further reduce carbon emissions associated with traditional power generation.

articleTitle: Novel Protection Scheme For UPFC Compensated Line
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The inclusion of Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) in long transmission line increases the transient and steady state stability. The conventional distance relaying technique finds difficulty to protect such UPFC compensated transmission line. Therefore, in this article a fast and reliable method is presented for fault detection and classification in a UPFC compensated line. The proposed method based on transient monitoring indexed three phase current for detecting fault and transient monitoring index assisted K-nearest neighbor (KNN) classifier for fault type identification. The evaluation of presented method is tested on a two machine 400 kV, 50 Hz UPFC compensated line developed in MATLAB/Simulink platform for several condition of power system like varying location, varying fault resistance and varied fault inception angle.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Distribution Transformer Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A distribution transformer fault refers to a malfunction or abnormal condition that occurs in a distribution transformer, which is a vital component in electrical power distribution systems. Distribution transformers lower high transmission voltage for use in homes and businesses. In this study, we address the critical challenge of transformer fault detection by employing a comprehensive approach that harnesses the power of advanced machine-learning techniques. We conducted extensive experiments utilizing a diverse dataset to predict and classify four distinct types of transformer faults. Leveraging the capabilities of twelve different classification algorithms, such as - SVM, DecisionTree(DT), AdaBoost, RandomForest(RF), ExtraTrees(ET), GradientBoosting(GB), MultipleLayerPerceptron(MLP), KNeighbors, LogisticRegression(LR), LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, XGBoost, and LGBM, we implemented a robust methodology that outperformed prior results, achieving a significantly higher accuracy rate. Key to our success is the integration of cross-validation, ensuring the reliability and generalization of our predictive models. This research advances the field of transformer fault prediction, offering a more accurate and dependable framework for identifying and mitigating critical issues in power distribution systems. The results hold substantial promise for enhancing the reliability and safety of transformer operations, with far-reaching implications for the energy industry.

articleTitle: Analysis of Genetic Algorithm-Optimized PID Controllers for a Two-Area Automatic Generation Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper aims to analyze an interconnected two-area Automatic Generation Control (AGC) power system through the application of optimization techniques based on Genetic Algorithm (GA). The principal objective is to enhance the overall system performance by optimizing the gain values of the three PID controllers using advanced optimization techniques like GA. This paper explores the overall performance by analyzing settling times in areas one and two and the deviation in tie line power. The system error is effectively minimized through the optimization of GA with the objective function of Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). Comparative analyses are conducted, comparing settling times in each area, tie line power deviation, and ITAE values with earlier simulated studies for a more comprehensive understanding to evaluate the novelty. The system is analyzed under two distinct loading conditions, analyzing each scenario individually in a case-by-case analysis. The article highlights the significance of the two-area AGC system and emphasizes the role of optimization techniques in elevating its performance, elucidating the substantial impact that optimization methods can bring.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis of Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper analyses a Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid (MG) model based on the IEEE 14-bus distribution system to determine various power quality parameters. The harmonic distortion of voltage and current is especially taken into account, caused by switching converters acting as an interface between the system and Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and the presence of nonlinear load. The crest factor is also analysed which is significant because it provides information about the dynamic range or fluctuations of a signal. The MG model is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis tool determines the voltage and current RMS. Values in the MG system for two different load levels- maximum load and 60% load.Passive filtering is the simplest and most used method for reducing harmonic distortion. In this study, a passive harmonic filter is designed to reduce harmonic distortion and to maintain IEEE standard limits of voltage and current harmonic distortions.

articleTitle: Empowering Remote Islands and Unlocking Sustainable Energy: A Hybrid Off-Grid DC System Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The interconnectedness of energy consumption and human progress is evident, but environmental challenges stemming from global energy production persist. Remote islands rely heavily on fossil fuel imports for power, yet green energy and decarbonization advances offer solutions. Overcoming nature’s unpredictability and weather dependence through the precise integration of renewables and converters is crucial. This study proposes a hybrid off-grid DC System for a remote site called ‘Fuerteventura’ in Spain, incorporating PV panels, wind turbines, converters, batteries, and diesel generators, addressing both electric and thermal loads. Simulation outcomes reveal its adaptability to the site climates, potentially elevating renewable use and curbing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions to achieve sustainable energy.

articleTitle: Synthetization of ZnO Nanostructured films prepared by Uncovered Hydrothermal Method for Textile Wastewater Cleaning Application
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The novelty of this work is to photodegrade the Textile wastewater using ZnO nanostructured films. The ZnO nanostructured films (Top layer) have been synthesized on the ZnO seed layer by a simple uncovered hydrothermal method at 85°C for 2 hr, whereas the ZnO seed layer is grown on a glass substrate by spin coating method for 3000 rpm and 15s. The structural properties of both the Top and seed layers of ZnO films showed a wurtzite structure with good crystallinity. The prepared ZnO films have a good absorption edge and bandgap energy within the range of 3.1~3.37 eV. The scanning electron microscope images exhibited nanorods (NRs)-like shapes, which have enhanced surface area and are more photoactive. Moreover, the photodegrading performance of the ZnO NRs films (Top layer) is more efficient than the spin-coated seed layer sample.

articleTitle: Transformer Protection Strategy During Solar Storm: Threat Analysis and Implementing Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Geomagnetic fluctuations have the potential to generate geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) within power transformers, which can result in equipment breakdown and power interruptions. The current investigation involves developing and experimenting with an RLC device to prevent geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) within the neutral part of a transformer. The device is designed to be compatible with the frequency range of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) and the impedance characteristics of the transformer neutral. The outcomes indicate that the RLC apparatus effectively restricted geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) from accessing the transformer, safeguarding it against potential harm. The mentioned apparatus holds significant potential as a crucial constituent of a comprehensive GIC safeguarding mechanism for power transformers, thus offering consistent power transmission to end-users. MATLAB-SIMULINK simulates how the RLC device blocks GIC from entering the power transformer.

articleTitle: Pre-Feasibility Study on Concentrated Solar Power Plant for Restructuring Power System in Urban Areas of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: A concentrated solar plant pre-feasibility study has been carried out in the present work to investigate its possible gradual impact on the power system restructuring process. A software based simulation study on optimization of concentrated solar plant and field level survey has been conducted for two different locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh for 1, 50 and 100 Megawatt power generation conditions. Our result indicates that small scale power generation can be a comparably cheaper solution. Integrating these power plants into the national grid can prove economically viable, while also addressing space limitations and fostering innovation in renewable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Hybrid Relaying Scheme For TCSC Compensated Line Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Due to changes in transmission line impedance, the standard distance relay primarily fails to safeguard the TCSC compensated line. Fault detection and classification is a challenging task in a TCSC line for conventional relaying scheme. This proposed technique is based on S-transform feature assisted ensemble bagging method and it is more preferable for such transmission line to overcome the issues of conventional techniques. This technique requires only three phase current for different pattern of fault on power network. This method is evaluated on a 500 kV, 350 km TCSC compensated network simulated by MATLAB /Simulink for various condition of power network like varying fault location, different fault resistance and varied inception angle etc. This proposed method is a fast and reliable technique for fault detection and classification of long series compensated line.

articleTitle: Faulted Line Identification in Power Network using Unsupervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Identification of faults in a power grid is crucial for maintaining stability of the network. Fault identification can help in operation of relays in the network and also provide real time information to network operators. In this paper, a machine learning based algorithm is proposed for faulted line identification in the network. Wide area measurement system (WAMS) provide synchronized data from different location in the network. This data is used for the proposed method. Principle component analysis (PCA) and k-means algorithm are used for faulted line identification in a power grid. The proposed method can identify fault conditions in the network and discriminate them from other stressed situations such as power swing. The method has been tested for the IEEE-9 bus network. The performance of the method is also tested with a renewable energy source in the network. The results obtained from PSCAD simulations highlight the accuracy of the proposed method in faulted line identification.

articleTitle: Hybrid ABC-PSO Algorithm based Static Synchronous Compensator for Enhancing Power System Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper introduces a Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony and Particle Swarm Optimization (HABC-PSO) approach for static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) implementation, aimed at improving system damping, addressing low-frequency and sub-synchronous oscillations, and enhancing overall power system stability. The proposed control strategy optimizes both the AC and DC voltage regulator’s proportional-integral (PI) of the STATCOM using a time-domain objective function. To assess the effectiveness of this control scheme, we conducted steady-state and transient analyses using a kundur multi-area four-machine model. The simulation results were analyzed to assess the generator’s rotor speed deviation, angle deviation, and bus-bar voltage deviation when using the HABC-PSO-based STATCOM. These results were then compared with scenarios both with and without the STATCOM, which included an examination of the settling times for rotor speed deviation (Δ ω) and angle deviation (Δ δ) of generators between the two areas. The simulation outcomes affirm that the proposed HABC-PSO based STATCOM is more resilient and efficient in mitigating inter-area oscillations, ultimately strengthening the power system stability.

articleTitle: A Local Electricity Model for DER Aggregator at a Distribution Network Level
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This Paper proposes a fully Decentralized Day ahead (DA) local electricity market (LEM) model which facilitates smooth market design in a restructured power System. LEM has local producers and consumers like PV, WT, DG and energy storage systems. The main objective of this model is to mark the challenge of integrating DERs into a grid that enables to trade energy with the operator at distribution level. As LEM involves DERs whose capacity is insufficient to incorporate a market model DER aggregator (AG) is one of the possible solutions. The proposed model involves a DA market where AGs submit their bids to DSO and the DSO clears the market at the lowest possible price by considering all technical constraints of the network. The Proposed model is evaluated through a case study of a modified 33-bus test system which shows effective energy trading at a distribution system with a considerable marginal range of violations.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Scheme for Efficient Power System Waveform De-noising and Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of modern power systems, the abundance of meters and digital communication technologies has led to an increase in data quality challenges, including noise and packet drops. This research paper introduces a deep learning model, specifically for the purposes of waveform de-noising and the reconstruction of missing packets in waveforms, with a focus on its application in power system power quality assessment. The proposed model’s performance was evaluated by comparing it with three established conventional approaches. Results demonstrate its superior capability in effectively de-noising the power system waveform and reconstructing missing data packets. Consequently, this model presents a valuable solution for enhanced power system monitoring and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Design & Analysis of Smart Agrivoltaic Monitoring System: Bangladesh Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This study proposes an agrivoltaic monitoring system that is designed based on land in Bangladesh. The simulation part of the study considers the rainy condition of the location to understand the impact on the energy harvesting of the system. The required amount of water for irrigation and the number of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels are calculated considering the rainfall and shadow impact, respectively. The study shows that the designed monitoring system utilizes a small amount of energy from the agrivoltaic system, where around 2665 PV modules can be set up on 1 hectare of land. A 1.5 kW pump is required, which has a flow rate of 120 L/min considering the rainfall of the area, to irrigate the land. The designed system can automatically turn on the irrigation based on the sensor data and can be controlled and monitored remotely.

articleTitle: Assessing Input-Side Current Distortion Caused by LED-Based AC Loads: An Experimental Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Understanding LED technology's impact on power quality is essential given the growth in the use of LED lighting applications. In electrical networks, harmonic distortion and other problems with power quality are exacerbated by the growth of non-linear loads like LED lighting systems. This paper focused on the impact of AC loads made of LEDs on input-side current distortion. This study focused on the impact of LED-based AC loads on input-side current distortion by conducting a thorough investigation of these loads. The experimental setup included integrating representative 5W and 9W LED loads into a regulated AC power system. Under a variety of operating circumstances, including various supply voltage and load levels, the levels of current distortion were measured. Harmonic content, total harmonic distortion (THD), power factor, and other pertinent metrics were investigated to determine the degree of current distortion. The experimental findings showed distinct current distortion patterns linked to the two types of LED loads. The harmonic components and distortion characteristics of the 5W LED load were distinct, whereas the input-side current effects of the 9W LED load were different. These results enable a deeper comprehension of the contributions to harmonics and power factors of LED-based AC loads and offer useful insights into the relationship between LED-based AC loads and power quality.

articleTitle: Finite Element modeling and analysis of lightning induced effects on a buried pipeline
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This work presents the 3D numerical modeling and analysis of lightning return stroke effects on a buried pipeline. A typical lightning impulse current is considered to strike on the ground and the associated channel current and the free space electromagnetic fields are thoroughly investigated first for the model validation. Then the model is used to investigate the lightning effects on the pipeline buried at different depths (1 – 5 m) and at different horizontal distances (0 – 10 m). As observed, the presence of buried metal pipe facilitates to induce higher current density on the surface of the pipeline, particularly when the ground conductivity is low. The current density reaches to as high as about 5000 A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the corresponding electric field is about 500 kV/m for a finite ground with conductivity 0.01 S/m. This is high enough to cause burn or physical damage in the pipelines. The electric field is also significantly influenced by the ground conductivity. As the conductivity decreases from 0.1 to 0.001 S/m, the electric field increases by the same order (from 50 to 5000 kV/m). Both the current density and the electric field decrease with the increase in the buried depth and the horizontal striking distance. It is expected that the proposed model and the presented investigation will be useful to develop the failure mechanism and so to design the protection plan of the buried pipelines.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Wind Deloading Estimation Approach for Frequency Control of a Renewable Integrated Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Large penetration of DFIG based wind system can have severe impacts on the frequency stability of the grid. Such wind power plant typically injects active power into the network through power electronic converters. Hence they are unable to engage actively in frequency enhancement by providing sufficient inertial or governor support during any unbalance condition. One possible solution can be to keep certain amount of power as deloaded reserve by increasing rotor speed, operating away from maximum power tracking curve. However, restriction on maximum allowable rotor speed can put a limitation on such reserve margin. By controlling the pitch angle, it is possible to maintain the rotor speed within acceptable range. To this end, this study proposes a novel methodology that develops a linear regression based mathematical relationship between deloading percentage and observed frequency response by utilizing a coordinated over speed and pitch angle controller. Through this way, proper deloaded reserve can be allocated to maintain sustainable system frequency. This approach is further analyzed on a modified IEEE 39 bus test grid in DIgSILENT PowerFactory software. Obtained outcomes indicate a linear correlation between lowest frequency point and deloaded reserve for a fixed wind penetration. Nonetheless, minimum required deloading percentage to ensure stable grid operation decreases with the increment in the wind integration percentage. Thus this approach can assist the grid operators to deploy proper wind deloading maintaining uninterrupted operation of the grid.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Testing a Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell Using Lagerstroemia Speciosa Natural Dye
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) promote the creation of photovoltaic devices with supreme transition efficiency and cheap rate in a system for converting clean and non-convectional solar power to electricity. An organic dye obtained from the Lagerstroemia speciose plant was used to fabricate DSSC. Owing to their excellent electron mobility and broad surface area, nano crystalline TiO2 placed on a glass substrate with fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) has been utilized in this study to be a dye absorber, and as a back electrode, a carbon contrast electrode was used. In this study, under AM 1.5 radiance, visual and surface configuration-based analysis of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film, and the photovoltaic cell performance parameters, the efficiency of solar cells of 0.1245%, short circuit current density of 0.42 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, open circuit voltage of 430 mV, and fill factor of 0.6945 were all attained.

articleTitle: On Possibilities of Using Tidal Stream Turbine for Power Generation in Karnaphuli River
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a MATLAB Simulink model for a Tidal Current Turbine. The model has been used to calculate the amount of power that can be generated from the port area of Karnaphuli river. Moreover, the required size of the tidal stream turbine has been calculated considering the site characteristics. Different calculated parameters were used as inputs for the mathematical model of tidal stream turbine. Based on the mathematical model, a model for Tidal Stream Turbine has been developed in MATLAB Simulink. The input parameters for this model were derived from the tidal current velocity data of Karnaphuli river and the mechanical design properties of the turbine. The simulation results showed that the tidal stream turbine system can generate approximately 1 MW from individual unit - the ideal generating capacity for which each generation unit was designed. However, the Simulink model doesn't take the system’s hydrodynamics into account. The findings of the system design show that it is possible to produce electricity from the tidal current velocities at Karnaphuli, Chittagong. The tidal plant’s economic value and cost analysis show that its overall energy costs are comparable to those of other tidal power plants currently in operation. With a proposal that data be acquired for specific places to estimate the power generating potential, this paper will help pave the way for additional research into the use of the nation’s tidal energy.

articleTitle: A Noncoupled Inductor Based Single-Phase AC-DC SEPIC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The noncoupled inductor ac-dc converters are in demand due to high voltage gain industrial applications. In this research study, a new noncoupled inductor single-phase ac-dc converter based on single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) topology is proposed. The proposed converter offers high step-up gain without the utilization of transformer. Following the IEEE-519 standards, the converter delivers a reduced input current total harmonic distortion (THD). In addition, the simplified circuit structure with only two switches significantly reduces switching loss and overall cost. Furthermore, the proposed converter offers high quality performance under sudden load change behavior. The terminology of the converter is demonstrated in MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Speed Vertical Wind Generator Charge Controller for Sustainable Energy Generation in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Integrating renewable energy is a great solution to mitigate the global energy demand. The windbased energy system has added a new dimension to the renewable energy system. In Bangladesh, solar-based energy generation systems are increasing rapidly. Large-scale windbased energy installation is still under research due to low wind speed. The available wind speed in Bangladesh is 5m/s on average in the coastal area. However, a 100W vertical axis wind generator starts working with 2m/s wind speed, while the rated speed is 11m/s. Therefore, a vertical-axis wind generator will be feasible for Bangladesh if the turbine can be designed with a low-speed range. In this work, a charge controller is designed and practically developed for a 100W vertical-axis wind generator. The availability of the windbased charge controller is very scanty in the market in Bangladesh. Besides the online charge controller price is comparatively high. Hence a cost-effective and efficient charge controller design is one of the main objectives of this work. In this work, a microcontroller-based wind charge controller is designed using Proteus professional software. The digital display system is integrated here to display the voltage and current reading. Finally, the developed charge controller is tested in the laboratory. The experimental results show the validity of the charge controller, which can convert the three-phase input signals to a DC signal to charge a battery and operate the DC loads successfully.

articleTitle: Green Hydrogen Production in Bangladesh: A Zero Carbon Initiative
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Efforts are being made worldwide to reduce carbon emissions in order to mitigate global warming. The production of hydrogen using renewable and sustainable energy sources could be an important step in zero carbon emission initiatives. This paper investigates the potential of solar–wind-battery based hybrid microgrid energy architecture for powering a hydrogen production plant to produce 150 kg of hydrogen daily. The plant is proposed to be located in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. The optimal solution of microgrid design is based on the criteria of energy costs, meeting demand requirements, and limiting excess electricity. The optimal design includes 2.6 MW of solar panels and five 100 kW wind turbines. This integrated system adeptly meets the target energy demand while demonstrating surplus electricity generation of 11.9% through a detailed analysis of various operational scenarios. The paper highlights the economic viability of the microgrid considering both installation and operating costs. The positive environmental impact is evident with an estimated reduction of around 2278 tons of carbon dioxide emissions, emphasizing its role in promoting green and sustainable energy practices.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Controller’s Stability for Multi-Area Power Systems with a Variety of Energy Sources Using Automatic Generation Control (AGC)
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The implementation of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) is crucial in the management of system frequency and tie-line powers within large-scale multi-area interconnected power systems, ensuring that these parameters remain at their designated nominal levels. The scope of our research is a thorough examination of the analysis of the Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller employed in the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) of multi-area power systems that integrate various sources of energy. The first phase of the study entails analyzing a reheat thermal power system with two areas, which exhibits a Generation Rate Constraint (GRC) that is deemed adequate. The utilization of optimization criteria is employed to formulate the design problem, with the aim of optimizing the requisite parameters of the PID controller. The efficacy of the proposed PID controller has been substantiated within the framework of the interlinked power system. Furthermore, the proposed technique has been expanded to include power systems comprising two regions, incorporating a variety of generation sources such as thermal, hydro, wind, and diesel units. The components encompassed under the system model include the boiler dynamics, the Governor Response Characteristic (GRC), and the Governor Dead Band (GDB). Upon comparing the simulation findings with those previously published in the literature, it is observed that the proposed approach exhibits superior dynamic responses in terms of performance. Moreover, the scope of the study encompasses three thermal power systems of varying areas, each equipped with unique controllers. The obtained results are then compared to the previously published findings on FA-optimized PIDD controllers for the same system being analyzed.

articleTitle: Designing a Backstepping Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Controller for PEMFC System Employing a DC-DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a backstepping integral terminal sliding mode control (BITSMC) system tailored to manage the DC-DC boost converter’s output voltage, solving the issue of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) low voltage output which seamlessly integrates the attributes of both integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC) and backstepping control (BC) by effectively mitigating the limitations associated with these individual controllers. The controller is crafted using a representative model of the DC-DC boost converter, primarily aimed at precisely following a predetermined reference output voltage. The stability of the tracked voltage is confirmed through control Lyapunov analysis. To evaluate its effectiveness, extensive simulations are conducted on a Matlab/Simulink platform by considering various operating conditions and that is compared with an existing ITSMC. The comparative analysis underscores the superiority of the suggested controller in the areas of quicker reference tracing and mitigation of issues such as overshoot, undershoot, and settling time.

articleTitle: A New Self-Balancing Five-Level Switch Capacitor Inverter for Standalone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new five level inverter self-balancing inverter which is applicable for renewable energy applications. The proposed inverter exhibits several unique features such as reduced switching devices, double boosting capacity, optimized total harmonic distortion. One group of the switching devices enables the self-balancing capacity while the other group works for providing a voltage of five level which as a whole enhances overall efficiency as well as reduces complexity. The voltage balancing circuit ensures a fixed voltage over the DC link capacitors, addressing common voltage balancing challenges encountered in multi-level inverters. By strategically activating a combination of specific switches, capacitors C1 and C2 are charged and discharged, allowing for precise control over the output voltage levels. The inverter associates a double boosting capability, significantly reducing the need for an external boost converter, therefore streamlining the system. An improved modulation technique is employed to minimize total harmonic distortion (THD), resulting in improved power quality and reduced switching losses. The calculation regarding the switching angle is also incorporated in this work. In conclusion, the presented self-balancing five-level inverter allows an innovative solution for renewable energy applications, characterized by reduced component count, enhanced voltage control, and improved modulation techniques. These characteristics make it a promising choice for efficient and reliable energy conversion in renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Enhancement of SmartGrid Stability by Optimal Energy Management System (EMS) through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Electrical power networks depend on power system stability to provide dependable and continuous operation. It speaks to a power system's capacity to continue operating in a balanced and steady manner after minor and major disruptions. The stability of the electricity system is necessary to avoid large-scale blackouts and guarantee that customers will always have access to energy. The most momentous obstacle to generating a steady flow of electricity at a low cost is the fluctuating pattern of generation, load, and demand. To address this problem, a day-ahead energy management system (EMS) based on deep learning has been proposed; it offers the necessary functionality to guarantee that the energy production systems balance stability levels at the lowest possible operational costs. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and CNN-Multilayer Perceptron (CNN-MLP) approach has been created for forecasting the accuracy level of electricity balance stability with the use of demand-side management (DSM). To improve outcomes, the dataset has been subjected to data analysis and feature scaling. The customer response time regarding the electricity production dataset, established statistical parameters, and minimum price elasticity coefficients (0.05–1) were examined in addition to the time-domain simulation findings to verify the stability of the power network. A score of 93.75% accuracy is offered by the proposed CNN-MLP model, whereas CNN delivers 93.55% accuracy. The outcome of this suggested optimized deep learning CNN-MLP predictive model, which uses the Adam optimizer, indicates that it is much more beneficial than the CNN predictive model in terms of properly monitoring the balance of power and providing it to clients at a reasonable price.

articleTitle: Integrating AE-CNN with Smart Relaying and SSCB for Enhanced Three-Phase Fault Detection and Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Amidst escalating demands for electricity, the complexity of power systems has significantly increased, making fault detection increasingly challenging. This research addresses the critical need for efficient fault detection and mitigation in three-phase power systems, proposing a novel solution integrating autoencoder-based Convolutional Neural Networks (AE-CNN) with Smart Relaying and Solid-State Circuit Breakers (SSCB). We developed and tested a Hybrid Neural Network model, trained with data processed from MATLAB simulations, to accurately detect faults in these systems. Our AE-CNN model achieved a remarkable 99.99% accuracy in fault detection, underscoring its effectiveness. Post-detection, the SSCB technology swiftly mitigated faults. This research not only demonstrates the precise detection and rapid mitigation of faults in three-phase power systems but also exemplifies the successful adoption of cutting-edge technologies. Our work makes a significant contribution to the evolution of modern power systems, offering a highly reliable and innovative solution to maintain the integrity and stability of electrical networks in the face of increasing complexities.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Home Energy Management System to Minimize Energy Consumption Cost in Peak Demand Hours
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative smart energy management system that makes use of IoT technologies. The system model allows for real-time monitoring, remote control, and cost analysis of electrical appliances, to improve energy efficiency and user convenience. Our work is distinguished by its innovative and practical approach, which provides a unique solution that tackles several facets of appliance management. Users obtain the opportunity to remotely monitor and operate the devices by combining hardware implementation with software integration, optimizing energy consumption and saving costs. To implement energy conservation, the system provides automated load scheduling with proactive user notifications. This research adds value to the development of smart energy management by providing the demand side management and demand response for sustainable energy consumption. This energy management is a seamless synergy of hardware, software, and IoT technologies demonstrating its potential to revolutionize residential energy management. It helps users make informed decisions about energy usage by providing a user-friendly interface and actionable insights aligned with global sustainability goals. Results show the reduction in daily load consumption without and with the optimization. The initiative not only demonstrates a practical application of energy-efficient living, but it also has potential for broader applications in smart home automation and energy-conscious lives.

articleTitle: Performance of Microgrid Systems on Multiple Dynamic Loads Penetration
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) have emerged as a promising solution to enhance the reliability and sustainability of modern power distribution systems. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in interconnecting multiple microgrids to create more resilient and efficient energy networks. However, the performance of interconnected microgrids under various dynamic load scenarios remains a critical research area. In this paper, problems like low-frequency oscillations (LFOs) and the dynamic performance of multiple induction motors (IMs) in microgrids instead of a single motor with the same rating under a wide range of operating conditions are looked at. A single microgrid and an interconnected microgrid are two alternative model configurations designed in Matlab/Simulink that are considered in this study’s comparison of non-linear dynamic simulations. The findings show that, compared to a local microgrid system, the performance of an interconnected microgrid system is more susceptible to being impacted by several parallel IM loads. Furthermore, it has been discovered that large IMs have lower LFO damping capabilities than parallel multiple small IMs.

articleTitle: Optimal Location Selection for Electric Vehicle Charging Points: Advancing Sustainable Urban Mobility in Dhaka
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This study investigates the crucial significance of optimal Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) location selection in advancing sustainable urban mobility in Dhaka. Dhaka city's challenges in transportation congestion and air quality represent the need for effective electric mobility solutions. To find the best EVCS sites, the study uses the Gravity model and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) methodologies. Both approaches lead to "Kamalapur" under "Motijheel" as the ideal location. This consistent finding reinforces its significance in serving the city's EV charging needs. The study highlights the importance of EVs in mitigating urban challenges, emphasizes the role of optimal EVCS locations, and showcases the effectiveness of the employed methods. Practical implications extend to informed urban planning and policymaking for sustainable mobility.

articleTitle: Impact of Grid-tied Battery to Grid (B2G) Technology for Electric Vehicles Battery Swapping Station
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles strains the grid. Implementing Battery Swapping Station (BSS) technology with distributed energy resources is a possible approach to alleviating this strain. Conventional grid-powered BSS confronts difficulties such as high electricity costs, grid instability, carbon emissions, etc., and BSS integrated with a microgrid may emerge as a promising solution for addressing these challenges. This technology will enable BSS to recharge batteries by utilizing distributed energy resources (DER), reduce the charging time for electric vehicles, and act as a microgrid power source for emergencies. This will assist in demand balancing and grid stability within the grid network. This paper assesses the effects of microgrid-based Battery to Grid (B2G) technology with BSS battery storage. The objective is to evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of B2G between microgrids and BSS, as well as its impact on the overall grid's stability and performance, along with the optimization of the power flow analysis. The result demonstrates that the integration of BSS with microgrids has the potential to provide substantial benefits for both Electric Vehicles (EVs) and the grid. BSS can play a crucial role in the future of transportation and energy with appropriate planning and implementation.

articleTitle: Autonomous Power Management and Control Among Interconnected Standalone Hybrid Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Multiple microgrids (MGs) being interconnected permits a high penetration of renewable energy sources while also improving the reliability and generation efficiency of the interconnected MG system. However, an effective power management strategy (PMS) and reliable control structure are required to ensure suitable operation and proper power sharing. Therefore, an effective clustering method of three hybrid MGs with a decentralized control structure is proposed in this paper to ensure sufficient power supply in three MGs depending on their available power generation in islanded mode. The interconnection takes place among the DC buses of each hybrid MG using a bidirectional DC/DC converter, which eliminates the complexity of reactive power management and synchronization and reduces power losses and costs. Moreover, the proposed decentralized PMS is based on the system voltage deviation to achieve proper power sharing without any communication link. Different scenarios for power sharing among interconnected hybrid MGs, including load variations, source failure, and energy storage systems charging or discharging, are analyzed. The performance of the proposed interconnection method and PMS is analyzed and validated using MATLAB/Simulink and a real-time-based OPAL-RT digital simulator. The simulation outcomes show that the proposed method and PMS ensure reliable operation and provide proper power sharing among the three hybrid MGs.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of PV System Integrating Thermoelectric Generators and Automatic Cleaning System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive design aimed at enhancing the efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems through the integration of thermoelectric generators (TEGs), automatic cleaning systems, and PV sun tracking mechanisms. TEGs are employed to capture and convert waste heat from PV panels into additional electricity, thus, increasing the system's output. The automatic cleaning system ensures that panels remain dust-free, mitigating performance degradation caused by dust accumulation. Concurrently, PV sun tracking maximizes energy captured by dynamically aligning panels with the sun's trajectory. The result shows through the proposed system, maximum energy capture of PV is ensured, which is 38.14% by maintaining surface cleaning, sun tracking, and optimizing the wastage of heat. A prototype was built to monitor the increase in efficiency in real life.

articleTitle: Improved Vector Control Scheme for Voltage Source Inverter Driven Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: With the growing adoption of renewable energy, solar photovoltaic (PV) based induction motor drives are gaining popularity. However, extraction of maximum power from solar PV arrays and high-performance control of induction motors poses significant challenges. This paper proposes a three-stage solar powered improved indirect vector controlled induction motor drive for optimal PV power harvesting and superior speed regulation. An incremental conductance (InC) maximum power point tracking algorithm and DC-DC buck converter rapidly extract peak power from the PV array under varying irradiation. A buck-boost converter maintains a steady DC voltage supply to the voltage source inverter (VSI) despite fluctuating PV output. Rotor flux-oriented indirect vector control of the induction motor decouples the torque and flux components in the stator current to achieve fast, accurate speed control similar to DC drives. Detailed modeling and simulation of the overall system is carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink platform. A small-scale experimental prototype is developed to verify the effectiveness of the scheme. The proposed improved controller overcomes the limitations of the conventional solar-powered scalar controlled and direct torque-controlled induction motor drives in terms of slower dynamics, torque pulsations, and limited speed range. This indirect vector control scheme demonstrates precise speed regulation and faster response due to independent flux and torque control in conjunction with maximum utilization of PV power.

articleTitle: Sustainability Assessment of Gaseous and Liquid Hydrogen Production Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Hydrogen is recognized as an emerging power generation fuel for the future since it emits significantly less amount of environmental impact compared with other conventional fossil fuels, such as natural gas and coal. Therefore, hydrogen fuel has attracted significant attention in its both gaseous and liquid state. However, these states have comparable impacts in terms of greenhouse gas emissions, climate change, human health, ecosystems, and resources. To the best of our knowledge, no work has been done to analyze the effects of gaseous hydrogen (GH) and liquid hydrogen (LH) states. This study has compared the environmental impact of GH and LH production processes. The life-cycle assessment is simulated in the environmental software SimaPro, version 9.5.0.1, using the ecoinvent 3 database applying ReCiPe 2016, Ecological scarcity 2021, IPCC 2021 GWP500, and Environmental Footprint 3.1 methods. Using the ReCiPe method GH and LHs’ environmental impacts are analyzed based on global warming, ozone formation, stratospheric ozone depletion, and ecotoxicity categories. It is observed that LH is more environment-friendly than GH in terms of human health, ecosystems, and resources achieving an impact score of 65%, 70%, and 42%, respectively when the maximum impact scores of corresponding GH parameters are set 100% for comparison. Energy resources, Global Warming, water pollutants and other impact categories are assessed for both GH and LH using the Ecological Scarcity 2021 method and GH has more impact than LH. Global Warming Potential for 500 years including CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> uptake measure using IPCC2021 GWP500 method and 27 environmental impact categories analyzed using Environmental Footprint 3.1 method. Moreover, GH has more environmental impact than LH in all impact categories except for ionizing radiation, freshwater ecotoxicity, and water consumption.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Based Energy Management System and Optimization for Seamless Integration of Renewable and Grid Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The substantial growth of both the industrial sector and the global population has resulted in a noteworthy upswing in worldwide energy consumption. This has underscored the imperative to investigate alternative energy sources and improve access to power. Microgrids present a compelling alternative by incorporating renewable energy sources and decreasing dependence on fossil fuels. This research introduces an Energy Management System (EMS) designed for microgrid applications, utilizing fuzzy logic principles. The goal is to enhance the efficient utilization of energy resources and streamline load management, ultimately contributing to the effective operation of microgrids. In this study, maximum power is extracted from photovoltaic and wind energy conversion systems, respectively, using Perturb and Observe (P&O) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The proposed approach enables seamless switching from the grid source to renewable sources within 0.1 ms when sufficient renewable energy surpasses the load demand. Moreover, if the load exceeds the predetermined tolerance value, the management system promptly disconnects the renewable source while ensuring continuous power supply.

articleTitle: Power Theft Detection in Residential Distribution Grids using Dirichlet Process Mixture Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In developing nations like India, distribution companies annually face a loss of billions of dollars due to electricity theft. Conventional manual inspection of power theft can be very time-consuming and ineffective. Hence, advanced methods need to be developed to accurately detect electricity theft. The technique proposed in this work is based upon irregular-scenario classification, feature extraction and clustering to identify suspicious customers. The proposed methodology makes use of Bayesian Non-Parametric Dirichlet Process Mixture Modelling (BNP-DPMM) which is an advanced clustering algorithm and eliminates the problem of having a fixed number of clusters. A rigorous analysis is carried out and the proposed technique successfully group irregular and regular customers in very distinct clusters. For verification, another analysis on actual Smart meter data is also carried out and the technique is able to again successfully categorize different types of customers in distinct clusters.

articleTitle: Data Quality Assessment of Substation Data in Bangladesh: Insights from Handwritten Data Digitization
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The assessment of power quality is vital for evaluating the existing state of the electricity supply, pinpointing its deficiencies, and guiding enhancements to guarantee a stable and consistent power supply, particularly in the face of rising demands from both industrial and residential sectors. In the context of Bangladesh, however, most substation data are still recorded manually, despite ongoing digitization efforts. This paper focuses on the quality of digitized transcription of handwritten substation data to determine its suitability for further analytical use. Our analysis revealed that the paper-based data from the substations exhibited significant gaps, undermining its reliability and accuracy. Through comprehensive evaluation, we concluded that the data, in its current state, is inadequate for in-depth analysis without the application of robust imputation methods. By tackling these challenges, our research aims to contribute to more informed decision-making and the efficient management of Bangladesh’s electrical infrastructure. This study not only diagnoses the current shortcomings in data quality but also lays the groundwork for future improvements in the country’s approach to energy data management.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Off-Grid Solar-Powered EV Charging Stations for Sustainable Transportation in Bangladesh – A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) hold significant importance in today's world due to their capability in reducing environmental pollution and their potential to ensure sustainable transportation. In Bangladesh, EV integration into the transportation system is also showing great potential. To this end, this paper presents a generalized methodology for designing and assessing the viability of off-grid solar-powered EV charging station (EVCS) in Bangladesh. The methodology considers weather profile of selected area, cost assessment, performance evaluation and environmental factor analysis, concurrently. To implement the method, the PVsyst platform is utilized. In this work, three Bangladeshi cities, namely Dhaka, Chittagong, and Rajshahi are selected to assess the feasibility of the proposed system. EVCS of 16.25 kWp, 19.50kWp and 35.80 kWp are considered in each site for the most appropriate selection of charging station. Moreover, different solar PV technology is also utilized to check performance of the proposed charging station. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted comparing the proposed station with a conventional fossil-fuel-based station. According to the findings, among the three systems studied, the off-grid 16.25 kWp system exhibits the best energy efficiency. The performance ratio for the EVCS in Dhaka city is found to be 0.771. With an impressive utilization rate of 93% and a total energy availability of 21,698 kWh, the system proves highly effective in utilizing solar power. Using monocrystalline modules is found to be advantageous, leading to increased energy production and overall economic benefits. The envisioned EVCS in Dhaka is capable of charging around 676 electric vehicles per year, each equipped with 30 kWh batteries. This results in a notable reduction of approximately 3,530 kg in carbon dioxide emissions. The research findings are expected to be valuable for decision-makers, researchers, and stakeholders in the transportation and renewable energy sectors in implementing eco-friendly transportation solutions in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: A ScPSO based Multi-Objective Approach for Optimal Placement and Sizing of multiple DSTATCOMs in Unbalanced Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Optimal DSTATCOM placement and sizing are crucial for power loss reduction, voltage profile improvement, balancing voltage, and economic burden alleviation on utility. Practical distribution networks are often unbalanced and finding optimal solutions with integrated devices requires an efficient algorithm. The standard PSO and ABC algorithms are slow and often stuck in local optima. This paper proposes a multi-objective Scout based PSO (MO-ScPSO) approach that integrates Scout phase of ABC into PSO. The approach is applied to achieve optimal DSTATCOM placement and sizing with the objective of reducing total real power loss, enhancing voltage profiles and mitigate voltage unbalance in the network and thus improving total annual cost savings. Simulations are conducted on the 25 – bus and IEEE 37 – bus test systems, demonstrating the proposed approach’s robustness and fast convergence rate.

articleTitle: Development of ‘South Asia Energy Database and Expert System’ for promoting Data Analytics and enhancing trade in the Regional Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: South Asia (SA) is amongst the fastest growing regions in the world and the energy demand in this region is continuously growing in a steep manner. In order to meet such a high level of growth, the electricity services in the region are required to be expanded with a still higher growth. The region has diverse energy resources as well as varied demand patterns. Under such situations, the energy trade amongst the different countries in SA can be of extreme importance towards optimization in the use of resources in the different countries as well as to bring overall economy and security at the regional level. To make the best use of the resources and the demand for diversity, the information plays a crucial role. The analytics in the form of Expert Systems can help convert this information into intelligence and action points. Taking into consideration these requirements, under USAID’s SARI/EI program, a digital energy database and knowledge resource platform, known as South Asia Energy Database (SAED), a first of its kind, has been developed and currently this platform is being operated and maintained by USAID’s other program South Asia Regional Energy Partnership (SAREP). This platform provides all relevant data related to the energy/power sector in the region at the click of a mouse and is working as a state-of-the-art, cloud-based data system on open-source software. This is equipped with very powerful analytics and reporting tools, through which a lot of intelligence and insights are added to the decision-making process, almost in real-time. This paper deliberates in detail, the objective behind the development of this utility, its design and architecture, the salient features of the expert system, deployment of the smart tools and analytics, and the advantages that are being derived from it by the different countries in South Asia, towards operation of the regional electricity grid, enhancement of the cross border electricity trade, as well as integration of the renewable and sustainable sources of energy in the different parts of the regional grid.

articleTitle: Clean Hydrogen Production from Floating Photovoltaics: A Case Study in Dhanmondi Lake, Dhaka
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Clean hydrogen is pivotal for reducing natural gas usage and advancing decarbonization. In this context, solar-based photovoltaic (PV) plants present a viable and eco-friendly approach to generating clean hydrogen energy. However, in densely populated countries like Bangladesh, the scarcity of available land necessitates the utilization of water bodies for PV installations, referred to as Floating PV systems (FPV). To this end, this paper proposes a novel methodology for assessing hydrogen generation through FPV systems in water bodies, taking into consideration technical, economic, and environmental concerns. The proposed methodology is implemented through the simulation of an FPV plant on Dhanmondi Lake, Dhaka, utilizing 1% of the total water body area as a conservative approach. The necessary simulations using PVsyst software demonstrate that the proposed FPV system with a capacity of 634 kWp, achieves a performance ratio (PR) of 77%. It generates an annual output of 925 MWh/year at a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.028 USD per kWh. Interestingly, this system can produce 149.6 tons of clean hydrogen annually through the PEM electrolyzation process. Furthermore, it significantly reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 12,900.88 tons and curtails water evaporation by 14,424 m³ per year. Over the lifespan of the project, the estimated social cost of carbon for the system amounts to 786,953.68 USD.
