The findings of this study highlight the promising potential of FPV-based hydrogen production, offering a cleaner and more cost-effective method of energy generation. This research can aid the researchers in developing models for future large-scale FPV-based hydrogen production endeavors in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: A Switched-Capacitor Multilevel Transformerless PV Inverter with MPC for Grid Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel switched capacitor-based inverter topology is proposed that produces five level auto boosted output voltage. Six switches, one dc voltage source, and one switching capacitor are utilized in this novel inverter. Notably, the capacitors’ voltage levels are kept in balance through direct charging from the input dc voltage source. Moreover, the leakage current issue is successfully resolved by creating a freewheeling path. This topology also reduces harmonic distortions in the inverter output voltage and grid current. To ensure accurate passing of active and reactive power to the grid, the system uses a model predictive control technique. The conduction modes, circuit description, and model predictive control algorithm to the suggested topology are covered in this paper. In addition, the comparison of the proposed inverter to various existing multilevel inverter topologies are discussed here. Simulation results validated in MATLAB/Simulink platform are represented in this paper. Additionally, experimental findings are also depicted here from a lab-built prototype that was put through a variety of tests in order to fully assess the effectiveness of the proposed inverter.

articleTitle: Eigenvalue sensitivity technique for optimal substitution of conventional generators with PV to meet the future goal of a renewable-dominant electrical grid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation is a fast-expanding renewable energy source at the worldwide level. When multiple conventional generators are on the verge of retirement, it becomes crucial to identify the critical generators that must be revived to provide the necessary inertial support, and the generators that can be replaced with PV without significantly compromising stability. The Eigenvalue sensitivity method is used to identify generators that positively or negatively impact the eigenvalue damping. In this paper, a sensitivity analysis of critical modes to the system inertia is utilized to maximize the replacement of conventional generators with PV plants without significantly impacting system stability. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is evaluated by means of both frequency domain and time domain analyses, and the results are compared with some other intuitive approaches for generator replacement. The studies have been carried out on the 68-bus 16-machine power system on the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Renewable Energy Based EV Charging Stations for Different Locations in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The market for electric vehicles (EVs) in Bangladesh consists mainly of electric bicycles, e-rickshaws and hybrid vehicles. The increased popularity of electric vehicles is leading to a greater pressure on the grid power supply due to their significant energy demand. Alternative energy sources that could be readily accessible and environmentally compatible need to be explored, given the needs of growing power demand in addition to environmental concerns and energy shortages. This study presents the techno-economic optimization of ecofriendly stand-alone solar-wind based electric vehicle charging stations in three different locations (Chattogram, Kuakata and Rangpur) in Bangladesh. For the comparison purpose, diesel generator and renewables based hybrid energy systems are also considered to find the environmental impact over renewable systems. A total of four off-grid configurations are investigated to find the best solution for EVs covering all aspects of technology, economy and environment. The results show that in terms of economy indicating Net Present Cost (NPC) and Cost of Energy (COE), the hybrid system PV-wind-diesel-battery is the optimal energy system for Chattogram and Kuakata. On the other hand, PV-diesel-battery shows the optimal solution for Rangpur. However, the systems with diesel generator emit a massive amount of carbon dioxide which is a major reason for environmental pollution. With regard to the size of the system components, as well as the associated NPC, COE, renewable fractions and carbon emissions, the overall impact on different locations is also different.

articleTitle: A Systematic Approach for Appropriate Selection of Electrode in Lithium-ion Batteries for Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Due to growing environmental concerns and rising fuel prices, electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining popularity over internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs). A growing emphasis is being placed on improving plug-in hybrid electric cars (PHEVs), which have a greater battery capacity and more flexible charging options than hybrid electric vehicles. In this regard, lithium-ion batteries are one of the most intriguing technologies whose performance largely depends on the choice of electrodes. Selecting the most appropriate electrode that maximizes battery performance while minimizing cost is essential for large-scale implementation. To this end, this paper proposes a systematic methodology to select the most suitable positive electrode technology for PHEV considering battery performance and cost aspects. Following the proposed approach, a total of 15 different types of electrodes are taken to calculate battery dimension, weight, energy density, and cost aspect in BatPaC software. Then, a normalized objective function is constructed to find the most appropriate positive electrode technology. In this research, the battery cost aspect is given the most weightage followed by other performance metrics. The findings show that, in terms of cost and performance, the NMC811-G (Energy) electrode provides the best result out of all the evaluated combinations. The proposed approach may be adapted to meet the needs of battery pack manufacturers for any type of EV technology. Therefore, this research can significantly aid in the selection of suitable electrodes for future lithium-ion batteries in the EV industry.

articleTitle: Reviewing a Few Challenges of the Dynamic Wireless Charging System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Dynamic electric vehicle (EVA) charging is a promising technology that allows automobiles to be charged while they are in motion, eliminating range anxiety and improving convenience. However, this novel charging mechanism is coupled with its difficulties. This paper explores some problems associated with dynamic EV charging systems including power loss due to misalignment, power control issues, energy transfer efficiency, etc. We have tried to do an in-depth review of these problems and have shown how these problems affect efficiency. This paper aims to discuss only the problems of dynamic EV charging systems so that future researchers and practitioners, build effective solutions and further advancements in dynamic EVA charging technology.

articleTitle: Evaluating Environmental Impacts and Proposed Solution for Temperature Effect of Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Solar energy plays a pivotal role in sustaining ecological balance and mitigating climate change. In this paper, the influence of environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, dust, and illuminance on the efficiency of solar panels were investigated through practical experiments. Also, a model to resolve the effect of increasing panel temperature was introduced to enhance the efficiency of PV panels. The proposed model incorporates a mist pump to alleviate temperature-induced efficiency loss, by dispersing mist-water droplets over the photovoltaic (PV) cells, consequently reducing their operational temperature. This, in turn, improves the energy conversion rate. However, a trade-off is made in this scenario because some of the energy produced is used by the pump.

articleTitle: An overview on Plant Energy: Unleashing the Potential of Trees as Green Electricity Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In the pursuit of sustainable and self-sufficient energy sources, recent scientific efforts have focused on tapping into the potential of living systems and biological structures. This study explores the remarkable electrical properties of the bilayer found in higher plant leaves, comprising cuticle and cellular tissue, which functions as an integrated triboelectric generator. This innovative mechanism enables the conversion of mechanical movements into electricity within living plants. Through detailed examinations using Kelvin force microscopy, the presence of induced and transported charges in living plant tissue is confirmed, while dead leaves of the same species show limited charge transport due to tissue dehydration. The research also highlights the possibility of using entire plants as "living triboelectric energy harvesters," demonstrating significant power outputs, reaching around ≈15 µW cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> *N, with variations based on plant species and leaf structure. Natural mechanical stimuli, such as wind, can also trigger triboelectric charges at the leaf, offering a promising "living plant-hybrid" prototype for harnessing wind energy. Considering these findings, trees, with their diverse species and extensive coverage, hold great promise as future electricity generators, contributing to eco-friendly technologies like wind-energy harvesting, planthybrid sensors, and other innovative plant-hybrid applications. Embracing this technology promotes a green future for electricity generation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Roof-Top Grid-Tied Solar Photovoltaic System in Textile Mill
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The depletion of global fossil fuel reserves has prompted a search for alternative energy to meet current demands. Solar power offers a clean,renewable,and eco-friendly solution. Yet,standalone solar systems are limited by seasonal variations. To counter this,integrated grid systems combining solar and conventional energy are being embraced. Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) estimates that utilizing solar energy from rooftops in Bangladesh's ready-made garments (RMG) and textile sector could yield 5000 MW. With over 7000 RMG factories and textile plants boasting ample rooftop space,about 400 MW could be generated using solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Although Bangladesh's total renewable capacity is 649.72 MW (2.93% of the total),mainly from solar home systems,the proposed rooftop initiatives promise reduced costs,heightened sustainability,and efficient space utilization. The paper presents the design and financial analysis of a major textile factory,unveiling substantial power usage and costs. It suggests a system of an average of 2,657,933 units per year resulting in a yearly saving in the electricity bill. The expected payback period is 4 years. Furthermore,performance analysis and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission reduction for an on-grid system have been explained in this paper. The initial cost of the system was calculated as 71,341,200 BDT and the payback period is 4 years. In addition,CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction in 25 year life span will be 56,481.075 tons.

articleTitle: Optimizing DC Motor Control via Leader Harris Hawks Algorithm with ITSE-ZLG Objective Function
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) controllers are widely employed to normalize the response of numerous DC motor-powered systems, such as electric locomotives, traction systems, etc. Specifically, this category of controller is ubiquitous due to their simplicity, ease of control, and low-cost. However, their design parameters need to be carefully tuned to enhance control performance. A novel LHHO-PID controller with a compound objective function that combine Integral of Time multiplied Squared Error (ITSE) with Zwee-Lee Gaing’s (ZLG) time-domain performance criterion is presented in this current study to enhance the control performance of a DC motor system. The system's performance was assessed by analyzing its response across various dimensions, including frequency responses, convergence profile and time. The results demonstrated that the developed PID-based controller exhibited a commendable performance in regulating the DC motor speed as compared to other existing PID-based controllers in the domain. The time response analysis showed an improvement of 7.2% compared to the best performing controller in rise time, a settling time of 0.1204 seconds, zero overshoot and negligible steady state error. These findings indicate that the proposed LHHO-PID controller has the capacity to regulate the speed of a DC motor efficiently in a variety of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of a Hybrid Off-Grid Microgrid to Power Saint Martin’s Island of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Bangladesh’s recent economic growth, fueled by the nation's fast development, has boosted the country's need for energy and increased its dependence on fossil fuels like coal and natural gas. This paper discusses the feasibility of a hybrid micro-grid for the effective exploitation of electricity in St. Martin, an island inside the Bay of Bengal located 34 kilometers from the mainland. By analyzing the performance of several configurations by combining different components and diverse characteristics, an ideal configuration was found using a methodological approach. Various features of the hybrid microgrid are examined and optimized in order to reach the best configuration. The study suggests PV/Wind/Battery/Diesel hybrid system as the ideal hybrid microgrid system. The design comprises the size and placement of the wind and solar energy generators, the size of the diesel engine, and the ability of battery to store energy. An efficient energy management system that maximizes the use of renewable energy sources, reduces dependency on diesel generation, and assures a steady and dependable power supply for the island’s users will receive special focus. The viability and sustainability of the selected microgrid is also evaluated in terms of sustainability – technical, economy, society and environment. The project’s feasibility has been assessed based on a number of factors, including the initial capital cost, operation and maintenance costs, and the decrease in greenhouse gas emissions. The suggested PV/Wind/Diesel/Battery hybrid microgrid might be used as a replicable model for other areas with comparable energy issues, advancing the development of resilient and sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: Decoding Smart Grid Equilibrium: Insights from Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In the complex landscape of smart grid stability, this study undertakes a detailed examination of machine learning models, assessing their effectiveness, interpretability, and predictive prowess in this essential sector. With Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Tree and Support Vector Machine appearing as the algorithms with the most promising results, this study emphasizes the necessity of bridging the gap between complex algorithms and useful, understandable solutions for efficient smart grid management. Shapley and LIME values act as illuminating agents, revealing the importance of different features, while ROC curves articulate the classifiers’ efficacy across various thresholds with elegance and precision. The outcomes of this investigation echo the promising capabilities of machine learning in enhancing smart grid stability, albeit necessitating cautious interpretation. These methods offer insightful revelations, underscoring their potential to not only enhance predictive accuracy but also facilitate a more nuanced understanding of the intricate variables influencing grid stability. The study underscores the imperative of bridging the gap between complex machine learning algorithms and practical, interpretable solutions to navigate the intricacies of smart grid management effectively. The findings encapsulate the resonating impact of machine learning, spotlighting its latent capability to transform the smart grid stability landscape while underscoring the essentiality of nuanced interpretation. In the expansive domain of energy management, explainable AI stands as a pivotal element, heralding a new era of clarity and innovation in the intricate world of grid management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Voltage Control in HESS-Based DCMG: A Comparative Analysis of SMC and PI Controllers
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Rising environmental awareness and reducing fossil fuel supplies are driving a move towards renewable energy sources. Microgrids, like DCMGs, offer a cost-effective way to improve energy stability and efficiency. It incorporates control algorithms to manage parameters like reliability and fault tolerance, aligning its operation with global standards. This study is conducted on the implementation and performance evaluation of a Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) to regulate voltage in a PV based DC microgrid. The aim is to improve the system's voltage stability and overall performance. Non-linear controllers offer superior adaptability and performance for fluctuating conditions in photovoltaic systems, compared to linear controllers. In this procedure, MATLAB/Simulink was employed to develop precise digital models for a HESS-based DC Microgrid, with a particular emphasis on SMC and PI controllers for bus voltage management. Both supercapacitors and batteries are employed for energy storage. Supercapacitors excel in rapid charge cycles and power density, while batteries offer superior long-term energy storage. The model was tested under varying load conditions at different time intervals to assess its adaptability and performance. In the study, SMC was developed and compared to conventional PI controllers for performance benchmarking. Through comparative evaluations, it was observed that SMC yielded a more consistent and stable voltage output than PI controller. This thorough analysis helps to explain the reason of using each control method in regulating the system.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Energy Storage Techniques Integration into Grid-Connected PV System for Green RMG Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Nowadays the Readymade Garments (RMG) sector is facing significant pressure to adopt sustainable energy solutions. The most suitable option for RMG owners to introduce renewable energy is the rooftop solar PV systems. However, the average sunlight (required for solar power generation) hours in a day is generally less than the average working hours of a typical RMG factory. Therefore, energy storage systems integrated with solar PV systems can ensure a sustainable, green, and efficient power supply during grid disruption, cloudy days, or even when there is not enough PV power output. In addition, energy storage can work as a backup power supply by replacing diesel generators and overall carbon emissions can be reduced. This paper aims to compare the techno-economic and environmental assessment of three different energy storage techniques integrated into grid-connected solar PV systems for a small RMG factory. Three distinct types of energy storage technologies are- lead-acid batteries, lithium-ion batteries, and supercapacitors. The Net Present Cost (NPC), Cost of Energy (COE), and Renewable Fraction (RF) are the main comparative indicators for this study. The comparative analysis shows that the PV-Grid system with Li-ion battery achieves the lowest COE and NPC compared to other storage-connected systems. From an environmental point of view, the renewable fraction for all three storage integrated systems can be around 40% which can reduce a huge amount of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: An Integral Sliding Mode Control of DC-DC Boost Converter Feeding CPLs in DC-Microgrids Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: This paper introduces a pulse width modulation (PWM) based Integral Sliding Mode Control (ISMC) technique for a DC-DC boost converter (DDBC), supplying power to the constant power loads (CPLs) in the renewable DC microgrids (DCMGs). In DCMGs, nonlinear CPLs and intermittent renewable energy sources (RESs) present a stability concern that is examined in this work. The ISMC utilizes the DDBC's nonlinear dynamical model to mitigate incremental negative impedance (INI), employing an advanced reaching law and an integral-based sliding surface for improved performance and robustness against the external disturbances. The global stability of the system is rigorously analyzed using control Lyapunov function theory. Comprehensive simulation studies including variations in input voltage, reference DC bus voltage, and power demand validate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the ISMC's advantages over the conventional dualloop proportional-integral (PI) control methods. The findings highlight the ISMC's effectiveness in maintaining stability and reliable performance amidst the challenges posed by CPLs and intermittent RESs in DCMGs.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation between Back-to-Back Converter and DC-DC Converter for Power Sharing Between Two Interconnected Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: As the voltage and frequency fluctuate concerning load or source power variations, it is necessary to maintain a predetermined nominal voltage and frequency to ensure stability and reliability in a microgrid system, particularly one that is operating in islanded mode. Nevertheless, introducing interconnection between microgrids ensures system stability and reliability by producing precise power flow management among microgrids. Hence, an infrastructure of interconnected microgrids using a back-to-back (BTB) converter has been proposed in this paper to integrate the microgrids operating in an islanded mode to maintain the prescribed limits of the system parameters, optimum power flow, and resilient operation during load fluctuation. The interconnected system with a BTB converter is designed in MATLAB/Simulink software with one converter controlled by DC-link voltage and the other by an AC voltage controller from microgrid-2 based on droop control and the system's performance is further evaluated using the OP5600-based OPAL-RT simulator. The findings demonstrate that aside from some switching losses, the proposed system incorporating a BTB converter provides effective power flow with minimal voltage and frequency fluctuations, making it a preferable choice compared to the DC-DC converter, which introduces significant ripples in power sharing and the energy storage system’s output, negatively impacting battery life.

articleTitle: Small Scale PV Integration in Bangladesh: Opportunities, Challenges, and Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: In the early 2000s, the Bangladesh government introduced nano and micro-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems in remote areas. As the power sector continues to grow, these nano-scale PV systems are becoming economically impractical. Additionally, the existing PV market policies are not sufficiently attractive to the mass population for installing small-scale PV systems known as SHS through private initiatives. This study aims to replicate the current SHS policies and pricing, assess the obstacles, and evaluate the economic viability of the current SHS system. Load profiles of three consumers are constructed and utilized to evaluate the economic feasibility of the existing system. Furthermore, various renewable-friendly policies, incentives, and net metering are applied to explore the economic viability of a modified system. The REopt tool is used to verify the economic feasibility, employing three hypothetical scenarios to assess the effectiveness of these policies and strategies in making SHS more appealing to the general population. Residential and small business load profiles are simulated using REopt. The findings of this research indicate that the implementation of net metering, combined with appropriate financial policies, can enhance the attractiveness of SHS to the mass population. These results provide valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders to shape future initiatives and promote the widespread adoption of small-scale PV systems in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Optimizing Residential Energy Consumption: Exploring Demand Side Management Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 10th IEEE International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Global demand for electrical energy is experiencing a steady increase on a daily basis. In order to address the growing demand, it is imperative to increase the generation capacity accordingly. The process of increasing generation capacity is a complex task that often involves the installation of new generating units, the modification of transmission lines, and the implementation of control systems, among other necessary measures. Furthermore, the escalation in power generation is associated with a corresponding rise in environmental pollutants. Demand Side Management (DSM) presents an alternative strategy that can effectively achieve a balance between energy demand and supply without requiring an increase in generation capacity. Moreover, the implementation of DSM has the potential to effectively reduce the usage of energy resources, thereby reducing environmental pollution. Residential buildings are a significant source of energy consumption, and DSM strategies offer numerous opportunities to optimize energy consumption in these buildings. This paper examines five DSM strategies applicable to residential consumers and discusses the potential benefits of each strategy. The strategies include the use of energy-efficient appliances, solar energy, load shifting, incentive-based peak clipping, and automated control of cooling loads. Results indicate that these DSM strategies are advantageous for reducing peak demand, total energy consumption, and energy costs. MATLAB software has been used for simulation and analysis.
